\title{Universal variational measure limits and a calibrated dual retraction\\on the actual analytic torus quotient}
\author{Unreviewed scoped progress on original P16.7}
\date{9 October 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
For every positive raw-mass-two Radon measure with finite full bounded
dual energy, every normalized bounded maximizing net has convergent
real energies, diagonal Monge--Ampere moments and actual weak
Monge--Ampere measures. The resulting measure is independent of the
maximizing net. Its full dual is exactly the limiting tangent dual,
and the original net maximizes that dual as well. Thus the construction
is an idempotent map of the finite-full-dual measure class, decreasing
dual energy and fixing every actual generated Monge--Ampere measure.
Moments of every fixed generated finite-energy weight also converge.
These results combine the separately qualified universal coercivity
and nonordered estimates; no domination of the prescribed measure is
assumed. Actual analytic representation of the limiting tuple, equality
of the constructed and prescribed measures, and prescribed-measure
existence remain unresolved. Original P16.7 is not declared solved.
\end{abstract}

\section{Actual object and qualified foundations}
Throughout use the actual compact Hausdorff analytic surface
\[
 K=\mathbb C((s)),\quad |s|=e^{-1/8},\quad t=s^8,
 \qquad X=(\mathbb G_m^2)^{\mathrm{an}}_K/
                  \langle(t,2),(3,t)\rangle.
\]
On injective torus charts let $r_i=-\log|z_i|$,
$\rho=|r|^2/2$ and $\theta=\DD\rho$. Affine logarithmic changes
of reference have zero $\DD$. The raw mass is
$\int_X\theta^2=2$. The original continuous class $\C$ includes
\emph{every stage} of the minimal continuous CLD psh sheaf:
$a\in\C$ means $\rho+a$ is in that sheaf locally.
Put $\theta_a=\theta+\DD a$, $\MA(a)=\theta_a^2$ and
\[
 E(a)=\frac13\int_X a\,[\theta^2+
                   \theta\wedge\theta_a+\theta_a^2].
\]
All measures below are actual Radon measures on $X$, not just
tropical images. In particular prescribed support is unrestricted.

The current qualified bounded calculus gives positive gradient
pairings $Q_T$ for positive closed $(1,1)$ currents, linear in $T$,
with Cauchy--Schwarz and the actual Green identity
\begin{equation}\label{green}
 Q_T(f,g)=-\int_X f\,\DD(gT)
         =-\int_X g\,\DD(fT).
\end{equation}
Continuous dpsh functions used here are in its strong-gradient domain;
the displayed differentiated currents are signed Radon when used in
this pairing. Constants, convex combinations and finite maxima
preserve $\C$. All bounded mixed products have raw mass two.
First variation, concavity, monotonicity and the tangent bound are
\begin{align}
 \frac{d}{dq}E((1-q)a+qb)&=\int_X(b-a)\MA((1-q)a+qb),\label{variation}\\
 E(b)&\le E(a)+\int_X(b-a)\MA(a),\label{tangent}\\
 E(0)&=0,\qquad E(a+c)=E(a)+2c.\label{constant}
\end{align}
The span of $\C$ is uniformly dense in $C(X,\R)$. Its qualification
is the actual separation proof in current409: small periodic smooth
weights separate tropical classes, and actual capped Laurent-polynomial
psh functions separate seminorms in one fibre. Constants and the
finite-maximum lattice formula then give lattice approximation.
No countable dense set is presumed.

For $C\ge0$ write
\[
 \C_C=\{a\in\C:\sup_Xa=0,\ E(a)\ge-C\}.
\]
The bounded mixed-moment estimates imply, whenever $p,q\in\C$, $p,q\le0$
have energies at least $-L$,
\begin{equation}\label{gradient}
 Q_{\theta_q}(p,p)\le6L,\qquad
 E^*(\MA(q))=E(q)-\int_Xq\MA(q)\le2L.
\end{equation}
Here
\[
 E^*(\mu)=\sup_{a\in\C}\left(E(a)-\int_Xa\,d\mu\right)
\]
is the \emph{full} original bounded dual. Finite dual for a positive
measure forces mass two by \eqref{constant}. For a measure of that
mass normalization by constants leaves the objective unchanged.

The new results use the complete bounded estimates of current411
and412, recalled precisely next. Their actual Green, Gauss,
finite-grid/point-atom and generated-calculus foundations remain
qualified analytic applications. This paper supplies the new
arguments below in full; it does not claim a new independent
recursive audit of all those foundations or of nonalgebraization.
The immediate CLD/GR applications and their original reading limits
remain attached to current407/409/411/412. A compiler, source identity
or historical verdict is not a mathematical premise.

\subsection{The two bounded inputs and the ordered generated input}
For $a,b\in\C_C$ define
\[
 I(a,b)=\int_X(a-b)(\MA(b)-\MA(a)).
\]
Green and the cubic energy identity give
\begin{equation}\label{midpoint}
 I(a,b)=Q_{\theta_a}(a-b,a-b)+Q_{\theta_b}(a-b,a-b)\ge0,
 \quad E((a+b)/2)-\frac{E(a)+E(b)}2=\frac{I(a,b)}8.
\end{equation}
Current412 supplies a finite nonnegative nondecreasing modulus
$H_C$, with $H_C(q)\to0$ as $q\downarrow0$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{endpoint}
 \int_X|a-b|\MA(a),\ \int_X|a-b|\MA(b)\le H_C(I(a,b)),
 \quad 0\le E(\max(a,b))-E(a),\ E(\max(a,b))-E(b)
               \le H_C(I(a,b)).
\end{equation}
The modulus comes from fixed finite calibrated Gauss grids and
smooth absolute-value approximations with continuous derivative
multipliers. For every fixed $w\in\C$ there is also a modulus
$J_{C,w}(q)\to0$ at zero for
\begin{equation}\label{fixed}
 \int_X|a-b|\MA(w)\le J_{C,w}(I(a,b)).
\end{equation}
For each actual point $x$ of total graded dimension two, its bounded
actual atom supplies $P_{C,x}(q)\to0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{point}
 |a(x)-b(x)|\le P_{C,x}(I(a,b)).
\end{equation}
These are separate fixed-$w$ and fixed-$x$ bounds; there is no uniform
bound asserted over all points or all tests.

Current411 gives \emph{universal} coercivity. If $B=E^*(\mu)<\infty$
and $a\in\C$ is normalized, then
\begin{equation}\label{coercivity}
 F_\mu(a):=E(a)-\int_Xa\,d\mu
 \le -c+1+B+\sqrt{6Bc},\qquad c=-E(a).
\end{equation}
This uses the actual Gauss bound $\int(-a)\theta^2\le1$ and
quadratic small-scale energy, not domination by bounded MA tests.
In particular $F_\mu(a)\ge-1$ implies
\begin{equation}\label{Cmu}
 -E(a)\le C_\mu:=\frac14
       \left(\sqrt{6B}+\sqrt{10B+8}\right)^2.
\end{equation}
For the scaling proof later, write $A=\int(-a)\theta^2$,
$q_0=Q_\theta(a,a)$, $q_1=Q_{\theta_a}(a,a)$.
All are nonnegative, and
\begin{equation}\label{cubic}
 -E(za)=zA+z^2(1-z/3)q_0+z^3q_1/3,
 \qquad -E(a)=A+2q_0/3+q_1/3.
\end{equation}

The actual generated class $\G$ consists of pointwise
$c_j\downarrow u$, $c_j\in\C$, $\inf_jE(c_j)>-\infty$.
Its actual energies, measures and moving moments are canonical in
current409. A finite-full-dual measure integrates every such $u$;
decreasing presentations converge in its $L^1$, with generated
pole sets null. If $p_j\downarrow u$, $p_j\le0$ and
$E(u)\ge-L$, the ordered estimate, extended by sequential
monotone convergence, is
\begin{equation}\label{ordered}
 \int_X(p_j-u)\MA(w)\le F_L(E(p_j)-E(u)),\qquad
 F_L(d)=3d+\sqrt{12L(9d/2+\sqrt{126Ld})},
\end{equation}
for every nonpositive bounded $w$ with $E(w)\ge-L$.
Here $F_L(d)\to0$ at zero and the constant is uniform over these
$w$. These qualified generated facts are used only for already
generated fixed weights, not to recognize a new nonordered limit.

\section{Uniform bounds and nonordered Cauchy control for every measure}
\begin{theorem}\label{universal}
Let $\mu$ be any positive mass-two Radon measure with
$B=E^*(\mu)<\infty$, and let $(a_\alpha)$ be any normalized net
in $\C$ with $F_\mu(a_\alpha)\to B$. Put
$\varepsilon_\alpha=B-F_\mu(a_\alpha)\ge0$.
On a tail all $a_\alpha\in\C_{C_\mu}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{deficit}
 I(a_\alpha,a_\beta)\le
             4(\varepsilon_\alpha+\varepsilon_\beta).
\end{equation}
There are real limits
\[
 E(a_\alpha)\to e,\qquad
 D_\alpha:=\int_X a_\alpha\MA(a_\alpha)\to D,
 \qquad \int_Xa_\alpha\,d\mu\to\ell=e-B.
\]
The net is Cauchy in $L^1(\MA(w))$ for every fixed bounded $w$,
and at every fixed total-dimension-two point. Its four moving
moving endpoint moments converge to $D$ when both indices tend
along this tail.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Since $F_\mu(0)=0$, $B\ge0$; a maximizing tail has objective
at least $-1$. Apply \eqref{Cmu}. For two terms on the tail the
midpoint is a full bounded competitor. Its measure term is affine,
so \eqref{midpoint} and its objective bound by $B$ give
$I/8\le(\varepsilon_\alpha+\varepsilon_\beta)/2$.
This proves \eqref{deficit} without any attainment assumption.

Put $C=C_\mu$ and $m=\max(a_\alpha,a_\beta)$.
Both $E(m)-E(a_\alpha)$ and $E(m)-E(a_\beta)$ lie in
$[0,H_C(I)]$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{energycauchy}
 |E(a_\alpha)-E(a_\beta)|\le H_C(I).
\end{equation}
This proves convergence of real energies without $L^1(\mu)$
convergence. Objective convergence then gives the signed integral
limit $\ell=e-B$.

For the diagonal moments set $f=a_\alpha-a_\beta$ and
$T=\theta_{a_\alpha}+\theta_{a_\beta}$.
The actual product transgression is
\[
 \MA(a_\alpha)-\MA(a_\beta)=\DD(fT),
 \qquad Q_T(f,f)=I.
\]
Decompose the diagonal difference as
\[
 D_\alpha-D_\beta=
 \int_X f\MA(a_\alpha)+
 \int_Xa_\beta(\MA(a_\alpha)-\MA(a_\beta)).
\]
The first integral has absolute value at most $H_C(I)$.
For the second, Green, Cauchy--Schwarz and \eqref{gradient}
give $|Q_T(a_\beta,f)|\le\sqrt{12CI}$.
Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{diagonalcauchy}
 |D_\alpha-D_\beta|\le H_C(I)+\sqrt{12CI}.
\end{equation}
Thus $D_\alpha$ is a real Cauchy net and converges to $D$.
Moreover
\[
 \left|\int_Xa_\alpha\MA(a_\beta)-D_\beta\right|
 \le\int_X|a_\alpha-a_\beta|\MA(a_\beta)\le H_C(I).
\]
Swapping indices gives both cross moments; both diagonal moments
already converge. All four joint-tail limits are $D$.
Finally \eqref{fixed} and \eqref{point} give the asserted Cauchy
properties and actual measurable $L^1$ limits by Banach completeness.
They do not assert that those measurable limits form a psh weight.
\end{proof}

\section{An actual canonical weak measure and its exact full dual}
\begin{theorem}\label{measure}
Under Theorem~\ref{universal}, the actual measures
$\MA(a_\alpha)$ converge weakly against every continuous function
to a positive mass-two Radon measure $\nu$. Its full dual is
\begin{equation}\label{dualnu}
 E^*(\nu)=e-D\le2C_\mu,
 \qquad E^*(\MA(a_\alpha))\longrightarrow E^*(\nu).
\end{equation}
Furthermore
\begin{equation}\label{calibration}
 \int_Xa_\alpha\,d\nu\to D,
 \qquad F_\nu(a_\alpha)\to E^*(\nu).
\end{equation}
All these limits are independent of the normalized maximizing net.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For fixed $w\in\C$, subtract its supremum and set
$L=\max(C_\mu,-E(w-\sup w),0)$. Constants disappear because
the endpoint masses agree. Transgression, Green and
\eqref{gradient} yield
\begin{equation}\label{weakbound}
 \left|\int_Xw(\MA(a_\alpha)-\MA(a_\beta))\right|
       \le\sqrt{12L\,I(a_\alpha,a_\beta)}.
\end{equation}
Thus every $\C$-test integral, and every finite linear combination,
is Cauchy. Uniform density of the span and common positive mass two
extend this to each $h\in C(X,\R)$: replacing $h$ uniformly by
a span element incurs total error at most $4\|h-h_0\|_\infty$
in a difference of integrals. The limits give a positive bounded
linear functional on $C(X,\R)$, taking $1$ to two. Compact
Hausdorff Riesz representation gives an actual positive Radon $\nu$.
This proves whole-net weak convergence without extracting a
subsequence or imposing metrizable/countable test hypotheses.

For each \emph{fixed} bounded competitor $b$, \eqref{tangent}
implies
\[
 E(b)-\int_Xb\MA(a_\alpha)\le E(a_\alpha)-D_\alpha.
\]
Pass to the established weak and real limits and take the full
supremum in $b$. It follows that $E^*(\nu)\le e-D$.
The right side is finite and at most $2C_\mu$ by
\eqref{gradient}; integrability of generated weights therefore
precedes their later use.

Fix an index $\alpha$ on the common energy tail and let $\beta$
tend to infinity in \eqref{weakbound} with $w=a_\alpha$.
Here $L=C_\mu$. Weak convergence and \eqref{deficit} give the
quantitative calibration
\begin{equation}\label{quantcal}
 \left|\int_Xa_\alpha\,d\nu-D_\alpha\right|
              \le\sqrt{48C_\mu\varepsilon_\alpha}.
\end{equation}
Together with diagonal convergence this proves
$\int a_\alpha\,d\nu\to D$. Consequently
$F_\nu(a_\alpha)\to e-D$. Each such objective is bounded above
by $E^*(\nu)$, proving the reverse inequality and
\eqref{dualnu}--\eqref{calibration}. Bounded tangent gives
$E^*(\MA(a_\alpha))=E(a_\alpha)-D_\alpha$, so its limit is
the same exact dual value.

For another normalized maximizing family $b_\gamma$ of the
\emph{same} $\mu$, both tails have the same bound $C_\mu$.
The midpoint proof applies to a term of each family, with
$I(a_\alpha,b_\gamma)\le4(\varepsilon_\alpha+
\varepsilon'_\gamma)$. Equations \eqref{energycauchy},
\eqref{diagonalcauchy} and \eqref{weakbound} show equality of
both real limits and all continuous measure-test limits. They also
identify each fixed-test $L^1$ limit and each full-point value limit.
This proves independence without a common cofinal indexing sequence.
\end{proof}

\section{Dual decrease, idempotence and actual generated fixed points}
Let $\mathfrak M$ be all positive mass-two Radon measures with
finite full bounded dual. Maximizing sequences exist from the real
supremum defining the dual. The preceding independence defines
\[
 \mathcal V:\mathfrak M\longrightarrow\mathfrak M,
 \qquad \mathcal V(\mu)=\nu.
\]
\begin{theorem}\label{retract}
For every $\mu\in\mathfrak M$,
\begin{equation}\label{retraction}
 E^*(\mathcal V(\mu))\le E^*(\mu),\qquad
 \mathcal V(\mathcal V(\mu))=\mathcal V(\mu).
\end{equation}
Every actual $\MA(u)$, $u\in\G$, is a fixed point. In particular
all bounded Monge--Ampere measures are fixed points. These conclusions
do not identify $\mathcal V$ with the identity on $\mathfrak M$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Keep a maximizing tail $a_\alpha$, put $C=C_\mu$, and let
$\ell_\alpha=\int_Xa_\alpha\,d\mu$. Formula \eqref{cubic}
gives $q_0\le3C/2$, $q_1\le3C$ and, for $0\le z\le1$,
\[
 \left|\frac{d^2}{dz^2}E(za_\alpha)\right|
      =2[(1-z)q_0+zq_1]\le6C.
\]
First variation at $z=1$ is $D_\alpha$. Taylor's formula with
its integral remainder therefore gives, for $0<h\le1$,
\[
 E((1-h)a_\alpha)\ge E(a_\alpha)-hD_\alpha-3Ch^2.
\]
Scaling preserves $\C$, so this is another full bounded competitor
for $\mu$. Subtracting its measure term gives
\[
 \varepsilon_\alpha\ge
     h(\ell_\alpha-D_\alpha)-3Ch^2.
\]
Pass to limits for fixed $h$ and then let $h\downarrow0$.
It follows that $\ell\le D$. Since
$\ell=e-E^*(\mu)$ and $E^*(\nu)=e-D$, this is exactly
the dual decrease in \eqref{retraction}.

By \eqref{calibration} the same normalized net maximizes the
full dual of $\nu$, and its MA measures already converge to $\nu$.
Theorem~\ref{measure} applied to $\nu$, with independence of
the maximizing family, therefore proves $\mathcal V(\nu)=\nu$.

Finally take an \emph{already generated} $u\in\G$ and an
actual continuous decreasing presentation $c_j\downarrow u$.
The qualified generated calculus gives $\mu=\MA(u)\in\mathfrak M$,
\[
 E^*(\mu)=E(u)-\int_Xu\,d\mu,
 \quad E(c_j)\to E(u),\quad
 \int_Xc_j\,d\mu\to\int_Xu\,d\mu,\quad
 \MA(c_j)\rightharpoonup\mu.
\]
Normalize $b_j=c_j-\sup_Xc_j$. Its objective is unchanged,
so $b_j$ is a normalized maximizing sequence for $\mu$, and its
MA measure is unchanged too. Definition and independence of
$\mathcal V$ give $\mathcal V(\mu)=\mu$.
The $b_j$ need not decrease; no decreasing presentation of a new
nonordered limit is assumed in this argument.
\end{proof}

\section{Convergence of all fixed generated moments}
\begin{theorem}\label{generatedmoment}
For every fixed $u\in\G$ and any maximizing net in
Theorem~\ref{universal},
\begin{equation}\label{gmoment}
 \int_Xu\MA(a_\alpha)\longrightarrow
                      \int_Xu\,d\mathcal V(\mu).
\end{equation}
Every displayed integral is finite. The bound used to pass from
continuous presentations of $u$ is uniform over the maximizing tail.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $c_j\downarrow u$ be an actual presentation and
$M=\sup_Xc_1$, a finite real number. Then $p_j=c_j-M\le0$
decreases to $v=u-M$. Choose
$L\ge\max(C_\mu,-E(v),0)$. The translation rule and energy
monotonicity ensure $E(p_j)\ge E(v)\ge-L$.
The bounded tests $a_\alpha\le0$ also have energies at least
$-L$. Apply \eqref{ordered} to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{uniformpresentation}
 0\le\int_X(c_j-u)\MA(a_\alpha)
       \le F_L(E(c_j)-E(u))\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
uniformly in $\alpha$ on the tail. The generated dual inequality
against $\MA(a_\alpha)$, using its uniformly bounded finite
full dual, proves that the $u$ integrals are finite; this also
justifies the sequential monotone passage in \eqref{ordered}.
The limit measure $\nu=\mathcal V(\mu)$ has finite full dual
by Theorem~\ref{measure}, so $c_j\to u$ in $L^1(\nu)$.
For fixed $j$, weak convergence gives
$\int c_j\MA(a_\alpha)\to\int c_j\,d\nu$.
First choose $j$ so that both its uniform error in
\eqref{uniformpresentation} and its $L^1(\nu)$ error are small;
then take $\alpha$ large for this fixed continuous $c_j$.
The triangle inequality proves \eqref{gmoment}.
This uses sequential convergence for the fixed presentation only;
it does not invoke measurable monotone convergence for arbitrary nets.
\end{proof}

\section{Precise remaining original gaps}
Universal coercivity and nonordered estimates now give canonical
real-energy, diagonal-moment, full-point-value, fixed-test-$L^1$ and
weak-MA limits for every finite-full-dual prescribed measure.
The canonical measure map is idempotent and fixes actual generated
MA measures. None of these conclusions constructs an actual USC
psh representative for the limiting full-point tuple, or proves
that such a representative is in the original $\G$.

In particular $\nu=\mathcal V(\mu)$ has not been shown equal to
the prescribed $\mu$ for every eligible measure. Equality of
$\mathcal V(\mu)$ and $\mu$ is a necessary condition for a generated
solution by Theorem~\ref{retract}; sufficiency is not asserted.
The signed convergence of $\int a_\alpha\,d\mu$ does not prove
$L^1(\mu)$ convergence of the weights. Nor does convergence of all
fixed generated moments justify an unproved moving unbounded moment
at a new nonordered analytic limit.

Adequate actual representation or a proved replacement, recognition
in the original finite-energy domain, suitable envelope/orthogonality
or variational perturbations, equality with every prescribed measure,
and the full existence-and-uniqueness theory at the original scope
remain open. GR decreasing-net closure applies only after actual
psh/USC representatives are supplied; GR limit statements do not
manufacture the missing upper regularization. Counts remain
16 of 42 original problems solved, 26 open, 97 historically accepted
scoped papers. This paper is UNREVIEWED, with no original closure
or new acceptance. Full primary bodies/pixels/books remain LOCALONLY;
the protected P16.4 editor stays open and unchanged.
\end{document}

\title{Universal variational measure limits and a calibrated dual retraction\\on the actual analytic torus quotient}
\author{Unreviewed scoped progress on original P16.7}
\date{9 October 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
For every positive raw-mass-two Radon measure with finite full bounded
dual energy, every normalized bounded maximizing net has convergent
real energies, diagonal Monge--Ampere moments and actual weak
Monge--Ampere measures. The resulting measure is independent of the
maximizing net. Its full dual is exactly the limiting tangent dual,
and the original net maximizes that dual as well. Thus the construction
is an idempotent map of the finite-full-dual measure class, decreasing
dual energy and fixing every actual generated Monge--Ampere measure.
Moments of every fixed generated finite-energy weight also converge.
These results combine the separately qualified universal coercivity
and nonordered estimates; no domination of the prescribed measure is
assumed. Actual analytic representation of the limiting tuple, equality
of the constructed and prescribed measures, and prescribed-measure
existence remain unresolved. Original P16.7 is not declared solved.
\end{abstract}

\section{Actual object and qualified foundations}
Throughout use the actual compact Hausdorff analytic surface
\[
 K=\mathbb C((s)),\quad |s|=e^{-1/8},\quad t=s^8,
 \qquad X=(\mathbb G_m^2)^{\mathrm{an}}_K/
                  \langle(t,2),(3,t)\rangle.
\]
On injective torus charts let $r_i=-\log|z_i|$,
$\rho=|r|^2/2$ and $\theta=\DD\rho$. Affine logarithmic changes
of reference have zero $\DD$. The raw mass is
$\int_X\theta^2=2$. The original continuous class $\C$ includes
\emph{every stage} of the minimal continuous CLD psh sheaf:
$a\in\C$ means $\rho+a$ is in that sheaf locally.
Put $\theta_a=\theta+\DD a$, $\MA(a)=\theta_a^2$ and
\[
 E(a)=\frac13\int_X a\,[\theta^2+
                   \theta\wedge\theta_a+\theta_a^2].
\]
All measures below are actual Radon measures on $X$, not just
tropical images. In particular prescribed support is unrestricted.

The current qualified bounded calculus gives positive gradient
pairings $Q_T$ for positive closed $(1,1)$ currents, linear in $T$,
with Cauchy--Schwarz and the actual Green identity
\begin{equation}\label{green}
 Q_T(f,g)=-\int_X f\,\DD(gT)
         =-\int_X g\,\DD(fT).
\end{equation}
Continuous dpsh functions used here are in its strong-gradient domain;
the displayed differentiated currents are signed Radon when used in
this pairing. Constants, convex combinations and finite maxima
preserve $\C$. All bounded mixed products have raw mass two.
First variation, concavity, monotonicity and the tangent bound are
\begin{align}
 \frac{d}{dq}E((1-q)a+qb)&=\int_X(b-a)\MA((1-q)a+qb),\label{variation}\\
 E(b)&\le E(a)+\int_X(b-a)\MA(a),\label{tangent}\\
 E(0)&=0,\qquad E(a+c)=E(a)+2c.\label{constant}
\end{align}
The span of $\C$ is uniformly dense in $C(X,\R)$. Its qualification
is the actual separation proof in current409: small periodic smooth
weights separate tropical classes, and actual capped Laurent-polynomial
psh functions separate seminorms in one fibre. Constants and the
finite-maximum lattice formula then give lattice approximation.
No countable dense set is presumed.

For $C\ge0$ write
\[
 \C_C=\{a\in\C:\sup_Xa=0,\ E(a)\ge-C\}.
\]
The bounded mixed-moment estimates imply, whenever $p,q\in\C$, $p,q\le0$
have energies at least $-L$,
\begin{equation}\label{gradient}
 Q_{\theta_q}(p,p)\le6L,\qquad
 E^*(\MA(q))=E(q)-\int_Xq\MA(q)\le2L.
\end{equation}
Here
\[
 E^*(\mu)=\sup_{a\in\C}\left(E(a)-\int_Xa\,d\mu\right)
\]
is the \emph{full} original bounded dual. Finite dual for a positive
measure forces mass two by \eqref{constant}. For a measure of that
mass normalization by constants leaves the objective unchanged.

The new results use the complete bounded estimates of current411
and412, recalled precisely next. Their actual Green, Gauss,
finite-grid/point-atom and generated-calculus foundations remain
qualified analytic applications. This paper supplies the new
arguments below in full; it does not claim a new independent
recursive audit of all those foundations or of nonalgebraization.
The immediate CLD/GR applications and their original reading limits
remain attached to current407/409/411/412. A compiler, source identity
or historical verdict is not a mathematical premise.

\subsection{The two bounded inputs and the ordered generated input}
For $a,b\in\C_C$ define
\[
 I(a,b)=\int_X(a-b)(\MA(b)-\MA(a)).
\]
Green and the cubic energy identity give
\begin{equation}\label{midpoint}
 I(a,b)=Q_{\theta_a}(a-b,a-b)+Q_{\theta_b}(a-b,a-b)\ge0,
 \quad E((a+b)/2)-\frac{E(a)+E(b)}2=\frac{I(a,b)}8.
\end{equation}
Current412 supplies a finite nonnegative nondecreasing modulus
$H_C$, with $H_C(q)\to0$ as $q\downarrow0$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{endpoint}
 \int_X|a-b|\MA(a),\ \int_X|a-b|\MA(b)\le H_C(I(a,b)),
 \quad 0\le E(\max(a,b))-E(a),\ E(\max(a,b))-E(b)
               \le H_C(I(a,b)).
\end{equation}
The modulus comes from fixed finite calibrated Gauss grids and
smooth absolute-value approximations with continuous derivative
multipliers. For every fixed $w\in\C$ there is also a modulus
$J_{C,w}(q)\to0$ at zero for
\begin{equation}\label{fixed}
 \int_X|a-b|\MA(w)\le J_{C,w}(I(a,b)).
\end{equation}
For each actual point $x$ of total graded dimension two, its bounded
actual atom supplies $P_{C,x}(q)\to0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{point}
 |a(x)-b(x)|\le P_{C,x}(I(a,b)).
\end{equation}
These are separate fixed-$w$ and fixed-$x$ bounds; there is no uniform
bound asserted over all points or all tests.

Current411 gives \emph{universal} coercivity. If $B=E^*(\mu)<\infty$
and $a\in\C$ is normalized, then
\begin{equation}\label{coercivity}
 F_\mu(a):=E(a)-\int_Xa\,d\mu
 \le -c+1+B+\sqrt{6Bc},\qquad c=-E(a).
\end{equation}
This uses the actual Gauss bound $\int(-a)\theta^2\le1$ and
quadratic small-scale energy, not domination by bounded MA tests.
In particular $F_\mu(a)\ge-1$ implies
\begin{equation}\label{Cmu}
 -E(a)\le C_\mu:=\frac14
       \left(\sqrt{6B}+\sqrt{10B+8}\right)^2.
\end{equation}
For the scaling proof later, write $A=\int(-a)\theta^2$,
$q_0=Q_\theta(a,a)$, $q_1=Q_{\theta_a}(a,a)$.
All are nonnegative, and
\begin{equation}\label{cubic}
 -E(za)=zA+z^2(1-z/3)q_0+z^3q_1/3,
 \qquad -E(a)=A+2q_0/3+q_1/3.
\end{equation}

The actual generated class $\G$ consists of pointwise
$c_j\downarrow u$, $c_j\in\C$, $\inf_jE(c_j)>-\infty$.
Its actual energies, measures and moving moments are canonical in
current409. A finite-full-dual measure integrates every such $u$;
decreasing presentations converge in its $L^1$, with generated
pole sets null. If $p_j\downarrow u$, $p_j\le0$ and
$E(u)\ge-L$, the ordered estimate, extended by sequential
monotone convergence, is
\begin{equation}\label{ordered}
 \int_X(p_j-u)\MA(w)\le F_L(E(p_j)-E(u)),\qquad
 F_L(d)=3d+\sqrt{12L(9d/2+\sqrt{126Ld})},
\end{equation}
for every nonpositive bounded $w$ with $E(w)\ge-L$.
Here $F_L(d)\to0$ at zero and the constant is uniform over these
$w$. These qualified generated facts are used only for already
generated fixed weights, not to recognize a new nonordered limit.

\section{Uniform bounds and nonordered Cauchy control for every measure}
\begin{theorem}\label{universal}
Let $\mu$ be any positive mass-two Radon measure with
$B=E^*(\mu)<\infty$, and let $(a_\alpha)$ be any normalized net
in $\C$ with $F_\mu(a_\alpha)\to B$. Put
$\varepsilon_\alpha=B-F_\mu(a_\alpha)\ge0$.
On a tail all $a_\alpha\in\C_{C_\mu}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{deficit}
 I(a_\alpha,a_\beta)\le
             4(\varepsilon_\alpha+\varepsilon_\beta).
\end{equation}
There are real limits
\[
 E(a_\alpha)\to e,\qquad
 D_\alpha:=\int_X a_\alpha\MA(a_\alpha)\to D,
 \qquad \int_Xa_\alpha\,d\mu\to\ell=e-B.
\]
The net is Cauchy in $L^1(\MA(w))$ for every fixed bounded $w$,
and at every fixed total-dimension-two point. Its four moving
moving endpoint moments converge to $D$ when both indices tend
along this tail.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Since $F_\mu(0)=0$, $B\ge0$; a maximizing tail has objective
at least $-1$. Apply \eqref{Cmu}. For two terms on the tail the
midpoint is a full bounded competitor. Its measure term is affine,
so \eqref{midpoint} and its objective bound by $B$ give
$I/8\le(\varepsilon_\alpha+\varepsilon_\beta)/2$.
This proves \eqref{deficit} without any attainment assumption.

Put $C=C_\mu$ and $m=\max(a_\alpha,a_\beta)$.
Both $E(m)-E(a_\alpha)$ and $E(m)-E(a_\beta)$ lie in
$[0,H_C(I)]$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{energycauchy}
 |E(a_\alpha)-E(a_\beta)|\le H_C(I).
\end{equation}
This proves convergence of real energies without $L^1(\mu)$
convergence. Objective convergence then gives the signed integral
limit $\ell=e-B$.

For the diagonal moments set $f=a_\alpha-a_\beta$ and
$T=\theta_{a_\alpha}+\theta_{a_\beta}$.
The actual product transgression is
\[
 \MA(a_\alpha)-\MA(a_\beta)=\DD(fT),
 \qquad Q_T(f,f)=I.
\]
Decompose the diagonal difference as
\[
 D_\alpha-D_\beta=
 \int_X f\MA(a_\alpha)+
 \int_Xa_\beta(\MA(a_\alpha)-\MA(a_\beta)).
\]
The first integral has absolute value at most $H_C(I)$.
For the second, Green, Cauchy--Schwarz and \eqref{gradient}
give $|Q_T(a_\beta,f)|\le\sqrt{12CI}$.
Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{diagonalcauchy}
 |D_\alpha-D_\beta|\le H_C(I)+\sqrt{12CI}.
\end{equation}
Thus $D_\alpha$ is a real Cauchy net and converges to $D$.
Moreover
\[
 \left|\int_Xa_\alpha\MA(a_\beta)-D_\beta\right|
 \le\int_X|a_\alpha-a_\beta|\MA(a_\beta)\le H_C(I).
\]
Swapping indices gives both cross moments; both diagonal moments
already converge. All four joint-tail limits are $D$.
Finally \eqref{fixed} and \eqref{point} give the asserted Cauchy
properties and actual measurable $L^1$ limits by Banach completeness.
They do not assert that those measurable limits form a psh weight.
\end{proof}

\section{An actual canonical weak measure and its exact full dual}
\begin{theorem}\label{measure}
Under Theorem~\ref{universal}, the actual measures
$\MA(a_\alpha)$ converge weakly against every continuous function
to a positive mass-two Radon measure $\nu$. Its full dual is
\begin{equation}\label{dualnu}
 E^*(\nu)=e-D\le2C_\mu,
 \qquad E^*(\MA(a_\alpha))\longrightarrow E^*(\nu).
\end{equation}
Furthermore
\begin{equation}\label{calibration}
 \int_Xa_\alpha\,d\nu\to D,
 \qquad F_\nu(a_\alpha)\to E^*(\nu).
\end{equation}
All these limits are independent of the normalized maximizing net.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For fixed $w\in\C$, subtract its supremum and set
$L=\max(C_\mu,-E(w-\sup w),0)$. Constants disappear because
the endpoint masses agree. Transgression, Green and
\eqref{gradient} yield
\begin{equation}\label{weakbound}
 \left|\int_Xw(\MA(a_\alpha)-\MA(a_\beta))\right|
       \le\sqrt{12L\,I(a_\alpha,a_\beta)}.
\end{equation}
Thus every $\C$-test integral, and every finite linear combination,
is Cauchy. Uniform density of the span and common positive mass two
extend this to each $h\in C(X,\R)$: replacing $h$ uniformly by
a span element incurs total error at most $4\|h-h_0\|_\infty$
in a difference of integrals. The limits give a positive bounded
linear functional on $C(X,\R)$, taking $1$ to two. Compact
Hausdorff Riesz representation gives an actual positive Radon $\nu$.
This proves whole-net weak convergence without extracting a
subsequence or imposing metrizable/countable test hypotheses.

For each \emph{fixed} bounded competitor $b$, \eqref{tangent}
implies
\[
 E(b)-\int_Xb\MA(a_\alpha)\le E(a_\alpha)-D_\alpha.
\]
Pass to the established weak and real limits and take the full
supremum in $b$. It follows that $E^*(\nu)\le e-D$.
The right side is finite and at most $2C_\mu$ by
\eqref{gradient}; integrability of generated weights therefore
precedes their later use.

Fix an index $\alpha$ on the common energy tail and let $\beta$
tend to infinity in \eqref{weakbound} with $w=a_\alpha$.
Here $L=C_\mu$. Weak convergence and \eqref{deficit} give the
quantitative calibration
\begin{equation}\label{quantcal}
 \left|\int_Xa_\alpha\,d\nu-D_\alpha\right|
              \le\sqrt{48C_\mu\varepsilon_\alpha}.
\end{equation}
Together with diagonal convergence this proves
$\int a_\alpha\,d\nu\to D$. Consequently
$F_\nu(a_\alpha)\to e-D$. Each such objective is bounded above
by $E^*(\nu)$, proving the reverse inequality and
\eqref{dualnu}--\eqref{calibration}. Bounded tangent gives
$E^*(\MA(a_\alpha))=E(a_\alpha)-D_\alpha$, so its limit is
the same exact dual value.

For another normalized maximizing family $b_\gamma$ of the
\emph{same} $\mu$, both tails have the same bound $C_\mu$.
The midpoint proof applies to a term of each family, with
$I(a_\alpha,b_\gamma)\le4(\varepsilon_\alpha+
\varepsilon'_\gamma)$. Equations \eqref{energycauchy},
\eqref{diagonalcauchy} and \eqref{weakbound} show equality of
both real limits and all continuous measure-test limits. They also
identify each fixed-test $L^1$ limit and each full-point value limit.
This proves independence without a common cofinal indexing sequence.
\end{proof}

\section{Dual decrease, idempotence and actual generated fixed points}
Let $\mathfrak M$ be all positive mass-two Radon measures with
finite full bounded dual. Maximizing sequences exist from the real
supremum defining the dual. The preceding independence defines
\[
 \mathcal V:\mathfrak M\longrightarrow\mathfrak M,
 \qquad \mathcal V(\mu)=\nu.
\]
\begin{theorem}\label{retract}
For every $\mu\in\mathfrak M$,
\begin{equation}\label{retraction}
 E^*(\mathcal V(\mu))\le E^*(\mu),\qquad
 \mathcal V(\mathcal V(\mu))=\mathcal V(\mu).
\end{equation}
Every actual $\MA(u)$, $u\in\G$, is a fixed point. In particular
all bounded Monge--Ampere measures are fixed points. These conclusions
do not identify $\mathcal V$ with the identity on $\mathfrak M$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Keep a maximizing tail $a_\alpha$, put $C=C_\mu$, and let
$\ell_\alpha=\int_Xa_\alpha\,d\mu$. Formula \eqref{cubic}
gives $q_0\le3C/2$, $q_1\le3C$ and, for $0\le z\le1$,
\[
 \left|\frac{d^2}{dz^2}E(za_\alpha)\right|
      =2[(1-z)q_0+zq_1]\le6C.
\]
First variation at $z=1$ is $D_\alpha$. Taylor's formula with
its integral remainder therefore gives, for $0<h\le1$,
\[
 E((1-h)a_\alpha)\ge E(a_\alpha)-hD_\alpha-3Ch^2.
\]
Scaling preserves $\C$, so this is another full bounded competitor
for $\mu$. Subtracting its measure term gives
\[
 \varepsilon_\alpha\ge
     h(\ell_\alpha-D_\alpha)-3Ch^2.
\]
Pass to limits for fixed $h$ and then let $h\downarrow0$.
It follows that $\ell\le D$. Since
$\ell=e-E^*(\mu)$ and $E^*(\nu)=e-D$, this is exactly
the dual decrease in \eqref{retraction}.

By \eqref{calibration} the same normalized net maximizes the
full dual of $\nu$, and its MA measures already converge to $\nu$.
Theorem~\ref{measure} applied to $\nu$, with independence of
the maximizing family, therefore proves $\mathcal V(\nu)=\nu$.

Finally take an \emph{already generated} $u\in\G$ and an
actual continuous decreasing presentation $c_j\downarrow u$.
The qualified generated calculus gives $\mu=\MA(u)\in\mathfrak M$,
\[
 E^*(\mu)=E(u)-\int_Xu\,d\mu,
 \quad E(c_j)\to E(u),\quad
 \int_Xc_j\,d\mu\to\int_Xu\,d\mu,\quad
 \MA(c_j)\rightharpoonup\mu.
\]
Normalize $b_j=c_j-\sup_Xc_j$. Its objective is unchanged,
so $b_j$ is a normalized maximizing sequence for $\mu$, and its
MA measure is unchanged too. Definition and independence of
$\mathcal V$ give $\mathcal V(\mu)=\mu$.
The $b_j$ need not decrease; no decreasing presentation of a new
nonordered limit is assumed in this argument.
\end{proof}

\section{Convergence of all fixed generated moments}
\begin{theorem}\label{generatedmoment}
For every fixed $u\in\G$ and any maximizing net in
Theorem~\ref{universal},
\begin{equation}\label{gmoment}
 \int_Xu\MA(a_\alpha)\longrightarrow
                      \int_Xu\,d\mathcal V(\mu).
\end{equation}
Every displayed integral is finite. The bound used to pass from
continuous presentations of $u$ is uniform over the maximizing tail.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $c_j\downarrow u$ be an actual presentation and
$M=\sup_Xc_1$, a finite real number. Then $p_j=c_j-M\le0$
decreases to $v=u-M$. Choose
$L\ge\max(C_\mu,-E(v),0)$. The translation rule and energy
monotonicity ensure $E(p_j)\ge E(v)\ge-L$.
The bounded tests $a_\alpha\le0$ also have energies at least
$-L$. Apply \eqref{ordered} to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{uniformpresentation}
 0\le\int_X(c_j-u)\MA(a_\alpha)
       \le F_L(E(c_j)-E(u))\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
uniformly in $\alpha$ on the tail. The generated dual inequality
against $\MA(a_\alpha)$, using its uniformly bounded finite
full dual, proves that the $u$ integrals are finite; this also
justifies the sequential monotone passage in \eqref{ordered}.
The limit measure $\nu=\mathcal V(\mu)$ has finite full dual
by Theorem~\ref{measure}, so $c_j\to u$ in $L^1(\nu)$.
For fixed $j$, weak convergence gives
$\int c_j\MA(a_\alpha)\to\int c_j\,d\nu$.
First choose $j$ so that both its uniform error in
\eqref{uniformpresentation} and its $L^1(\nu)$ error are small;
then take $\alpha$ large for this fixed continuous $c_j$.
The triangle inequality proves \eqref{gmoment}.
This uses sequential convergence for the fixed presentation only;
it does not invoke measurable monotone convergence for arbitrary nets.
\end{proof}

\section{Precise remaining original gaps}
Universal coercivity and nonordered estimates now give canonical
real-energy, diagonal-moment, full-point-value, fixed-test-$L^1$ and
weak-MA limits for every finite-full-dual prescribed measure.
The canonical measure map is idempotent and fixes actual generated
MA measures. None of these conclusions constructs an actual USC
psh representative for the limiting full-point tuple, or proves
that such a representative is in the original $\G$.

In particular $\nu=\mathcal V(\mu)$ has not been shown equal to
the prescribed $\mu$ for every eligible measure. Equality of
$\mathcal V(\mu)$ and $\mu$ is a necessary condition for a generated
solution by Theorem~\ref{retract}; sufficiency is not asserted.
The signed convergence of $\int a_\alpha\,d\mu$ does not prove
$L^1(\mu)$ convergence of the weights. Nor does convergence of all
fixed generated moments justify an unproved moving unbounded moment
at a new nonordered analytic limit.

Adequate actual representation or a proved replacement, recognition
in the original finite-energy domain, suitable envelope/orthogonality
or variational perturbations, equality with every prescribed measure,
and the full existence-and-uniqueness theory at the original scope
remain open. GR decreasing-net closure applies only after actual
psh/USC representatives are supplied; GR limit statements do not
manufacture the missing upper regularization. Counts remain
16 of 42 original problems solved, 26 open, 97 historically accepted
scoped papers. This paper is UNREVIEWED, with no original closure
or new acceptance. Full primary bodies/pixels/books remain LOCALONLY;
the protected P16.4 editor stays open and unchanged.
\end{document}

9 October 2026. UNREVIEWED; original P16.7 OPEN.

1. A uniform third-test absolute moment bound.

Fix C>=0. For normalized a,b,w in C with all three energies >=-C,
write f=a-b and I=I(a,b). Paper412's smooth absolute-value Green proof
gives, for the actual positive Radon measure MA(w),

 int |f| MA(w) <= Omega_C(I)
    + (sqrt(Q_theta_w(w))+sqrt(Q_theta(w))) sqrt(Psi_C(I)),
 Psi_C(q)=q/2+sqrt(42Cq).

Both w-slot gradient energies are <=6C by the actual bounded mixed
moment bounds. Thus the SAME modulus

 K_C(q)=Omega_C(q)+2sqrt(6C) sqrt(Psi_C(q))

works for EVERY w on this energy sublevel, not only one fixed w.

It uses only continuous derivative multipliers of smooth approximations

\begin{abstract}
On the actual analytic quotient used in the current P16.7 packet, we
prove that a small cubic-energy midpoint deficit forces small absolute
moving moments against both endpoint Monge--Ampere measures, and small
energy gains under finite maximum. No order between the endpoints is
required. The proof fixes constants using actual coordinate Gauss fibres
and finite Gauss grids. It also gives uniform energy bounds for
variational maximizing nets for arbitrary prescribed mass-two measures
dominated by finite sums of bounded Monge--Ampere tests. Such nets are
Cauchy against each fixed bounded test and at every full-dimensional
point. These are actual bounded-weight estimates, not an analytic
representability theorem for their limits. Nonordered compactness,
obstacle orthogonality, and the full prescribed-measure equation remain
unresolved. No supplied verdict is a premise. The full historical
source audit requested by the operator is not completed here.
\end{abstract}

\section{Exact carrier, class, and source boundary}
Let $K=\mathbb C((s))$, $|s|=e^{-1/8}$, $t=s^8$, and use the
actual analytic quotient
\[
 X=(\mathbb G_m^2)^{\mathrm{an}}_K/\langle(t,2),(3,t)\rangle,
 \qquad \tau=(-\log|z_1|,-\log|z_2|).
\]
The deck transformations translate $\tau$ by $\mathbb Z^2$.
Rectangles of widths less than one give ordinary open injective
quotient charts, the compact unit polyannulus covers the quotient,
and only finitely many deck graphs meet two bounded boxes. Local
analytic gluing along these etale chart overlaps constructs $X$;
the diagonal is closed, since locally it is a finite union of closed
deck graphs. This uses the conventional analytic quotient gluing and
coherent descent of Conrad--Temkin, Lemmas 4.2.3--4.2.4, on finite
chart covers, not on the infinite covering map. Thus the carrier used
below is compact Hausdorff, good, smooth, separated, boundaryless,
and pure of dimension two. The present estimates use no algebraization
of $X$. The packet's nonalgebraization argument is retained separately
as unverified DATA, rather than counted as a completed new source audit.

On each chart put $\rho=|\tau|^2/2$, $\theta=\DD\rho$. A change
of lift changes $\rho$ by a smooth affine logarithm of a unit.
Let $\mathscr P$ be the \emph{entire} minimal continuous CLD psh
sheaf containing the ordinary smooth psh functions and closed under
local uniform limits, and define
\[
 \C=\{a\in C(X,\R):\rho+a\in\mathscr P\text{ locally}\},
 \theta_a=\theta+\DD a,\quad B(a,b)=\theta_a\wedge\theta_b,
 \MA(a)=\theta_a^2.
\]
No first-stage identity or global smooth psh approximation is assumed.
Constants, convex combinations, and finite maxima preserve $\C$:
smooth convex nondecreasing composition proves this for smooth slots;
uniform continuity and the minimal-sheaf argument extend one slot at a
time. CLD 8.2.4 states the corresponding local continuous composition
rule. Reference changes are the smooth $\DD$-null changes permitted
by CLD 8.8.5.

The exact published inputs are as follows. CLD 15.7.1 puts a separated
pure $n$-dimensional analytic space, with its analytic boundary, in the
calibrated tropical calculus. CLD 8.5.1 gives $u_jT_j\to uT$ for
positive currents $T_j\to T$ and continuous $u_j\to u$ locally

Smooth cutoffs and scalar approximation are the conventional

We never use arbitrary-multiplier closedness from CLD 8.6.7.

\section{All-stage bounded Green and energy, reconstructed}
For a positive closed $(1,1)$ current $T$, complete compact smooth
$(1,0)$ forms in the positive semidefinite pairing
$\int\alpha\wedge J\beta\wedge T$, locally using nonnegative
smooth cutoffs. Let $H_T$ consist of continuous functions with locally
uniform smooth approximants whose gradients converge strongly in all
these local seminorms. A uniformly zero sequence with a strong
gradient limit has zero gradient: pairing with a compact smooth form
$\beta$ gives, by closedness,
\[
 \int d'f_j\wedge J\beta\wedge T
 =-\int f_j d'(J\beta)\wedge T\longrightarrow0.
\]
The differentiated smooth coefficient has a finite measure on its
compact support; smooth Hilbert tests are dense. Partitions and
Leibniz patch local approximants. Bounded continuous multipliers act
by scalar approximation with norm bound $\|h\alpha\|\le
\|h\|_\infty\|\alpha\|$.

For $f\in H_T$ with $L_Tf=\DD(fT)$ signed Radon, smooth
approximation in both slots gives
\[
 \int gL_Tf=-Q_T(f,g),\qquad
 Q_{T,\chi}(f)=\tfrac12\int f^2\DD\chi\wedge T-\int\chi fL_Tf.
\]
The sheaf of $f\in H_T$ with $L_Tf\ge0$ contains smooth psh
functions and is locally uniformly closed. Indeed, for a uniformly
convergent sequence $f_j$ in this sheaf, choose cutoffs $\chi,\eta$,
$\eta=1$ near $\operatorname{supp}\chi$, and $|f_j|\le B$ on the
\emph{whole} support of $\eta$. With $\epsilon=\|f_j-f_k\|$ there,
positivity and the identity above give
\[
 Q_{T,\chi}(f_j-f_k)\le
 \tfrac12\epsilon^2\|\DD\chi\wedge T\|_{\rm TV}
 +2B\epsilon\|\chi\|_\infty\|\DD\eta\wedge T\|_{\rm TV}.
\]
Thus gradients are strongly Cauchy. Diagonal smooth approximants
and distributional positivity prove closure. Minimality includes
every continuous psh stage. Differences and finite patching give
\begin{equation}\label{green}
 Q_T(f,g)=-\int f\DD(gT)=-\int g\DD(fT),\qquad Q_T(f)\ge0
\end{equation}
for continuous dpsh functions on $X$.
Smooth $C^1$ one-variable composition with bounded derivative has
the strong-gradient chain rule, because uniform convergence of
the approximants gives uniform convergence of their derivative
multipliers, while their gradients converge strongly. This rule
uses continuous multipliers only.

Exact product terms have zero integral against $1$ by boundaryless
Stokes, so every $B(a,b)$ has the reference mass $M=2$, established
geometrically below. Define
\[
 E(a)=\tfrac13\int a[\theta^2+B(a,0)+\MA(a)].
\]
Cubic expansion and \eqref{green} give, for $a_t=(1-t)a+tb$,
\begin{equation}\label{variations}
 E'(a_t)=\int(b-a)\MA(a_t),\qquad E''(a_t)=-2Q_{\theta_{a_t}}(b-a).
\end{equation}
Hence $E$ is concave and monotone, $E(0)=0$, $E(a+c)=E(a)+2c$,
and
\begin{equation}\label{cocycle}
 E(b)-E(a)=\tfrac13\int(b-a)[\MA(a)+B(a,b)+\MA(b)].
\end{equation}
For $a\le b$, each nonnegative integral on the right is at most
$3(E(b)-E(a))$. The tangent inequality yields
\[
 D(\MA(q))=E(q)-\int q\MA(q),\quad
 D(\mu)=\sup_{p\in\C}\left(E(p)-\int p\,d\mu\right).
\]
Constants force mass two for a positive measure with finite $D$.
If $p,q,r\le0$ have $E\ge-C$, the nonnegative terms of $-3E(q)$
give $D(\MA(q))\le2C$, whence
\begin{equation}\label{moments}
 \int(-p)\MA(q)\le3C,\quad \int(-p)B(q,r)\le6C,
 \quad Q_{\theta_q}(p)\le6C,\quad Q_\theta(p)\le6C.
\end{equation}
For the mixed bound use $B(q,r)\le2\MA((q+r)/2)$ and concavity.
For the gradient bound use
$Q_{\theta_q}(p)=\int(-p)B(p,q)-\int(-p)B(0,q)$.

\begin{lemma}\label{alltest}
For nonpositive $a,b,w\in\C$ of energies at least $-C$, put
$f=a-b$ and $I=\int f(\MA(b)-\MA(a))$. Then
\[
 I=Q_{\theta_a}(f)+Q_{\theta_b}(f)\ge0,\qquad
 Q_{\theta_w}(f)\le\Psi_C(I),\quad
 \Psi_C(t)=t/2+\sqrt{42Ct}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Set $g=(a+b)/2$, $h=w-g$. Product transgression gives
$Q_{\theta_w}(f)-I/2=Q_{\theta_a}(f,h)-Q_{\theta_b}(f,h)$;
both sides have the signed expression $-\int f\DD f\wedge\DD h$.
Since $|h|\le-w+(-a-b)/2$, \eqref{moments} bounds the MA moments
of $|h|$ by $6C$ and its mixed moments by $12C$.
Expanding
\[
 Q_{\theta_a}(h)=-\int h[B(a,w)-(\MA(a)+B(a,b))/2]
\]
gives $Q_{\theta_a}(h)\le12C+3C+6C=21C$, and the same holds
with $b$. Direct-sum Cauchy--Schwarz proves the result.
\end{proof}

\section{Gauss normalization and actual fibre comparisons}
Let $S$ be the joint coordinate Gauss section modulo the deck group,
$S\simeq\R^2/\mathbb Z^2$. It is used to fix constants, not to
restrict prescribed measure support.

\begin{lemma}\label{gauss}
For $a\in\C$ the function $g_a(r)=a(\sigma(r))$ is separately
$1/2$-Lipschitz for circle distances, $a(x)\le g_a(\tau(x))$, and
$\sup_Xa=\max_Sa$. Consequently, if $\sup_Xa=0$, then
$-1/2\le a|_S\le0$. The actual measure $\theta^2$ is twice
Lebesgue measure on $S$, so its raw mass is two.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Fix $r_2$ and pass to the actual $z_2$ Gauss fibre
$\mathbb G_{m,\mathscr H(\eta_{e^{-r_2}})}^{\rm an}(z_1)$.
The analytic map sets $z_2$ to its canonical nonzero residue-field
element. Classical functoriality applies. The pulled-back local
weight glues to $\Phi(q)=q^2/2+r_2^2/2+g_a(q,r_2)$.
On an annulus $b\le q\le c$, subtract the affine interpolation
of its endpoint Gauss values. GR 6.4 bounds the difference by zero,
so $q^2/2+g_a(q,r_2)$ is finite convex. Period one gives subgradient
bounds $q-1/2\le p\le q+1/2$ using the secants to $q\pm1$.
Local absolute continuity gives $|\partial_qg_a|\le1/2$ almost
everywhere. Swap the coordinates for the other bound. Their combined
oscillation on the two circles is at most $1/2$.
Small rectangular polyannuli around an arbitrary $x$ have four
joint Gauss Shilov vertices. GR 6.4 bounds $(\rho+a)(x)$ by their
largest value. Shrinking the rectangle proves $a(x)\le g_a(\tau(x))$.

If $x$ is not coordinate Gauss, a Laurent polynomial $P=\sum c_Iz^I$
has strict cancellation $|P(x)|<\max|c_Iz^I(x)|$. This persists
on an ordinary neighborhood, where at least two terms realize
the maximum. Coordinate tropicalization there lies in a finite
tropical hypersurface of dimension at most one. The coordinate
$(2,2)$ form $\theta^2$ vanishes there by the CLD moment-form
dimension rule. Its measure is therefore supported on $S$.
On $S$, identity moments have saturated tangent lattice, degree one,
and calibration one by CLD 14.5.2--3. CLD 5.10.1--2 identifies the
Radon measure with the calibrated tropical integral. The Hessian of
$|r|^2/2$ is the identity; its raw wedge factor is $2!$, giving
density $2\,dr_1dr_2$. Quotient gluing gives the asserted measure.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{paths}
For each finite grid $\mathscr D_N=(N^{-1}\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z)^2$
and its base vertex $o$, there are finitely many fixed nonpositive
$w_l\in\C$ and a finite $A_N$ such that, for every continuous dpsh $f$,
\[
 |f(\xi)-f(o)|\le A_N\max_l\sqrt{Q_{\theta_{w_l}}(f)}
 \qquad(\xi\in\mathscr D_N).
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Connect the vertices to $o$ by coordinate-radius paths. Each path
uses one coordinate at a time and partitions into finitely many
injective tropical boxes. In a horizontal piece with fixed $r_2$,
CLD 18.6.2 with $d=1$, $f=z_2$, $t=1$ states
\[
 T_{r_2}=\DD\max(0,\log(|z_2|/e^{-r_2}))
 =\delta_{z_2^{-1}(\eta_{e^{-r_2}})}.
\]
This is the integration current of the actual curve over its Gauss
residue field; that field is unchanged throughout this one piece.
The source space is separated, boundaryless, equidimensional; the
coordinate morphism is smooth of relative dimension one. These are
precisely the corollary's hypotheses. Its immediate proof uses the
relative curvature/intersection formula of 18.6.1 and the intersection
coefficient one on the Gauss fibre. No variable section is asserted
analytic, and no finite-extension degree is inserted.

Let $\rho_0$ be a centered quadratic reference on the box.
The finite continuous psh $\psi=\max(0,\log(|z_2|/e^{-r_2}))$
is bounded on its compact closure. Choose an inner ball containing
the piece, an outer collar, and $\delta,\epsilon>0$ so that
$w=\max(0,\delta+\epsilon\psi-\rho_0)$ is positive on the inner
ball and zero on the outer collar. This is possible by making the
inner ball smaller than the outer one and $\epsilon$ sufficiently
small. Its reference weight is a maximum of continuous psh slots;
it extends by zero to $\C$. Inside, $\theta_w=\epsilon T_{r_2}$.
A cutoff $0\le\chi\le1$, one on the path, gives
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f)\ge\epsilon\int_{\mathbb G_{m,\mathscr H(\eta)}}
          \chi\,d'f\wedge d''f.
\]
For smooth ambient $f$, its radial restriction on this actual curve
is piecewise smooth. Unit log norms on a compact annulus have finite
piecewise affine radial presentations. Canonical degree-one calibration
makes radial gradient energy $|\partial_q f|^2dq$, and other curve
branches contribute nonnegative energy. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore
bounds the squared endpoint difference by $\ell/\epsilon$ times
$Q_{\theta_w}(f)$, where $\ell$ is the finite radial length.
The same fibre-current inequality for differences of local smooth
approximants proves strong convergence of their curve gradients;
uniform convergence gives endpoints. Thus the bound holds for all
continuous dpsh $f$ in the reconstructed strong domain. Sum the
finitely many $\sqrt{\ell/\epsilon}$ over each path, take a maximum,
and subtract finite constants from the caps. Vertical pieces use $z_1$.
\end{proof}

\section{New nonordered absolute moments and finite maxima}
Put $\C_C=\{a\in\C:\sup_Xa=0,\ E(a)\ge-C\}$, $C\ge0$.
For the fixed grids above let
$C_N=\max(C,\max_l[-E(w_l)],0)$ and define
\[
 \Omega_C(t)=\min\left(1,\inf_{N\ge1}
       \{4/N+4A_N\sqrt{\Psi_{C_N}(t)}\}\right),\qquad
 H_C(t)=\Omega_C(t)+\sqrt{6C}
       \left(\sqrt t+\sqrt{\Psi_C(t)}\right).
\]
These finite geometric constants are independent of the pair of
weights. For any fixed $N$ the second term tends to zero as $t\to0$;
then $N\to\infty$ proves $\Omega_C(t),H_C(t)\to0$.

\begin{theorem}\label{nonordered}
For arbitrary, not necessarily ordered, $a,b\in\C_C$, let
$f=a-b$, $I=\int f(\MA(b)-\MA(a))$, and $m=\max(a,b)$.
Then
\begin{align*}
 E((a+b)/2)-(E(a)+E(b))/2&=I/8,\\
 \int|f|\theta^2&\le\Omega_C(I),\\
 \int|f|\MA(a),\ \int|f|\MA(b)&\le H_C(I),\\
 0\le E(m)-E(a),\ E(m)-E(b)&\le H_C(I).
\end{align*}
For a fixed nonpositive bounded $w\in\C$, with $C'=\max(C,-E(w),0)$,
\[
 \int|f|\MA(w)\le\Omega_C(I)+
 \bigl(\sqrt{Q_{\theta_w}(w)}+\sqrt{Q_\theta(w)}\bigr)
              \sqrt{\Psi_{C'}(I)}.
\]
All these statements concern actual continuous weights and actual
analytic measures, including nonskeletal bounded test measures.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
In \eqref{variations}, $Q_{\theta_{a_t}}(f)$ is affine in $t$.
Twice integrating the second derivative at $t=1/2$ gives exactly
$(Q_{\theta_a}(f)+Q_{\theta_b}(f))/8=I/8$.

The restrictions $g_a,g_b$ are each coordinate $1/2$-Lipschitz,
so $f|_S$ is coordinate $1$-Lipschitz. Every point of $S$ has
circle-$\ell^1$ distance at most $1/N$ from a grid vertex.
Lemmas \ref{alltest} and \ref{paths} give
\[
 \operatorname{osc}_S f\le2/N+2A_N\sqrt{\Psi_{C_N}(I)}.
\]
Normalization $\max_Sg_a=\max_Sg_b=0$ implies
$\min_Sf\le0\le\max_Sf$, so $\|f\|_{C(S)}$ is at most this
oscillation. Multiplication by the mass two gives the bound
$4/N+4A_N\sqrt{\Psi_{C_N}(I)}$ for $\int|f|\theta^2$.
Also $|f|\le1/2$ on $S$, giving the bound one. Infimize over $N$.

Here is the absolute-value Green step with its precise justification.
Set $F_\epsilon(q)=\sqrt{q^2+\epsilon^2}$. Its derivative is continuous
and bounded by one; $F_\epsilon(f)$ lies in each strong-gradient
domain and $Q_R(F_\epsilon(f))\le Q_R(f)$. We need no assertion
that $\DD(F_\epsilon(f)R)$ is Radon. Green pairs it with the fixed
signed Radon $\DD(aR)$. Since
$\MA(a)-\theta^2=\DD(a(\theta_a+\theta))$,
\[
 \int F_\epsilon(f)\MA(a)
 \le\int F_\epsilon(f)\theta^2+
 \sqrt{Q_{\theta_a}(f)Q_{\theta_a}(a)}+
 \sqrt{Q_\theta(f)Q_\theta(a)}.
\]
Uniform convergence of $F_\epsilon(f)$ to $|f|$ passes each
integral against its finite signed measure. There is no indicator
multiplier or assumed strong absolute-value limit.
Now $Q_{\theta_a}(f)\le I$, $Q_\theta(f)\le\Psi_C(I)$, and
both $a$-slot energies are at most $6C$ by \eqref{moments}.
This proves the $a$ endpoint bound; use $b$ for the other.
Use the same argument with $w$ instead of $a$ for the fixed-test bound.

Monotonicity and the tangent inequality at $a$ give
\[
 0\le E(m)-E(a)\le\int(m-a)\MA(a)
 =\int(b-a)_+\MA(a)\le H_C(I).
\]
The other endpoint is identical. No minimum or infinite maximum
is inserted in the psh class.
\end{proof}

\section{Actual full-dimensional point consequences}
For clarity the point-atom input and its ordered consequence are
reconstructed here, rather than imported as a note grant.
At a total graded-dimension-two point $x$, Abhyankar excludes a
nonzero support kernel in the Laurent polynomial ring. Completion of
$K(z_1,z_2)$ adds no initials, since smaller-error approximation
preserves an initial form. Initial Laurent polynomials generate its
graded field by fractions; select two homogeneous independent ones,
represented by $P_1,P_2$. Their image is the weighted Gauss point of
radii $|P_i(x)|$, for arbitrary positive real radii. The source is
boundaryless, the target is reduced of dimension two, and the image
has graded dimension two. CLD 11.6.5(c) gives local finite flatness;
11.6.3 gives a compact local representative of rank $D>0$ with
singleton Gauss fibre. These exact immediate units were read.

On a neighborhood where the $P_i$ are units, the pleasant moment
has calibrated degree $D$ by CLD 14.5.2--3. For
$\psi=\max(0,\log(|P_1|/|P_1(x)|),\log(|P_2|/|P_2(x)|))$,
soft-max approximants on the plane have gradient image the standard
simplex of area $1/2$; the raw factor $2!$ gives mass one concentrated
at the origin. The calibrated upstairs mass is $D$. Properness and
the singleton Gauss fibre turn concentration in the target into
concentration at the actual $x$ against every continuous upstairs
test. Local uniform continuity of products gives $(\DD\psi)^2=D\delta_x$
locally. Equivalently this is CLD 18.6.2 with $d=2$.
Cap it by $\max(\rho_0,\delta+\epsilon\psi)-\rho_0$ on a small
injective tropical ball, zero on an outer collar, and extend by zero.
At polynomial zeros capped smooth logarithms are constant; soft
maxima give the continuous psh class on the whole ball. On an inner
neighborhood the curvature is $\epsilon\DD\psi$. Thus some actual
$w_x\in\C$ satisfies $\MA(w_x)\ge\alpha_x\delta_x$, $\alpha_x>0$.
The whole measure has finite $D$ by the bounded tangent formula;
no finite-dual assertion for its isolated Dirac component follows.

For nonpositive ordered $p\le q$ with energies at least $-L$ and a
fixed nonpositive test $w$ of energy at least $-L$, let
$d=E(q)-E(p)$. Then \eqref{cocycle} gives $I(p,q)\le3d$.
For $T=\theta_w+\theta_p$ and $k=w-p$, transgression and Green give
\[
 \int(q-p)\MA(w)\le3d+\sqrt{Q_T(q-p)Q_T(k)}.
\]
Lemma \ref{alltest} gives $Q_T(q-p)\le3I/2+\sqrt{42LI}$;
\eqref{moments} gives $Q_T(k)=I(p,w)\le12L$. Therefore
\[
 \int(q-p)\MA(w)\le F_L(d),\qquad
 F_L(d)=3d+\sqrt{12L(9d/2+\sqrt{126Ld})}.
\]
Apply this to $a\le m$, $b\le m$, with
$L_x=\max(C,-E(w_x-\sup w_x),0)$, and use
Theorem \ref{nonordered}. It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{point}
 |a(x)-b(x)|\le 2F_{L_x}(H_C(I))/\alpha_x\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{as }I\to0.
\end{equation}
This holds simultaneously as a separate bound at each actual full
point. It asserts no uniform bound in $x$ or analytic representative
of a limiting tuple.

\section{Prescribed-measure variational consequences without assumed attainment}
For a positive Radon measure $\mu$ of raw mass two define
$\mathcal F_\mu(a)=E(a)-\int a\,d\mu$. This is invariant under
constants. If $D(\mu)<\infty$, put
$D_C(\mu)=\sup_{a\in\C_C}\mathcal F_\mu(a)$, so
$0\le D_C(\mu)\le D(\mu)<\infty$.

\begin{corollary}\label{maximizing}
If $a,b\in\C_C$ have deficits
$\varepsilon_a=D_C(\mu)-\mathcal F_\mu(a)$ and
$\varepsilon_b=D_C(\mu)-\mathcal F_\mu(b)$, then
$I(a,b)\le4(\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_b)$.
Consequently every maximizing net on $\C_C$ is Cauchy in
$L^1(\MA(w))$ for every fixed $w\in\C$, and Cauchy at every
full-dimensional point. Its maximum energy gains tend to zero.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The midpoint $h=(a+b)/2$ has $E(h)\ge-C$, $\sup h\le0$.
Normalizing $h-\sup h$ preserves its functional and increases its
energy, so it is in $\C_C$. Linearity of the measure term and the
exact midpoint formula imply
\[
 I/8=\mathcal F_\mu(h)-
       (\mathcal F_\mu(a)+\mathcal F_\mu(b))/2
 \le(\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_b)/2.
\]
Use Theorem \ref{nonordered} and \eqref{point}. A maximizing net
exists as an approximation to the real supremum; no maximizer is
assumed. The argument uses no countable dense set or full-support
Radon measure on $X$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{coercive}
Suppose $\mu\ge0$, $\mu(X)=2$, and
$\mu\le\sum_{l=1}^k\beta_l\MA(w_l)$ for fixed bounded
$w_l\in\C$, $\beta_l>0$. This is domination of a prescribed
measure, not the assertion $\mu=\MA(u)$. Then $D(\mu)<\infty$,
and every normalized net maximizing the \emph{full} bounded dual
eventually lies in one fixed $\C_C$. Hence all the nonordered
Cauchy consequences of Corollary \ref{maximizing} hold for that net,
including $L^1(\mu)$ convergence and convergence of its real energies.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Normalize each $w_l$ and put $c_l=-E(w_l)\ge0$,
\[
 A_l=\sqrt6\bigl(\sqrt{Q_{\theta_{w_l}}(w_l)}+
                         \sqrt{Q_\theta(w_l)}\bigr).
\]
For normalized $a\in\C$, set $e=-E(a)\ge0$.
Gauss normalization gives $\int(-a)\theta^2\le1$.
Transgression against $w_l$ and Green, followed by \eqref{moments}
with energy bound $\max(e,c_l)$, yield
\[
 \int(-a)\MA(w_l)\le1+A_l\sqrt{\max(e,c_l)}
 \le1+A_l\sqrt{c_l}+A_l\sqrt e.
\]
Thus, with $B_0=\sum\beta_l(1+A_l\sqrt{c_l})$,
$B_1=\sum\beta_l A_l$,
\[
 \int(-a)\mu\le B_0+B_1\sqrt e,\qquad
 \mathcal F_\mu(a)\le-e+B_0+B_1\sqrt e
 \le B_0+B_1^2/4.
\]
Constants permit normalization of every competitor, proving finite
full dual. Its supremum is at least zero. On any maximizing tail
$\mathcal F_\mu(a)\ge-1$, so
\[
 e\le C_\mu=\left(\frac{B_1+
                \sqrt{B_1^2+4(B_0+1)}}2\right)^2.
\]
Apply the midpoint argument directly with the full supremum, using
midpoints as full competitors, and then the nonordered estimates
with $C=C_\mu$. Domination gives $L^1(\mu)$ Cauchyness as well.
Completeness of the Banach spaces $L^1$ gives actual measurable
limits for each test measure. The energies converge because
$E(a)=\mathcal F_\mu(a)+\int a\,d\mu$ and both terms converge.
These measurable limits are not identified with a generated analytic
weight; no such identification is hidden in Banach completeness.
\end{proof}

\section{Exact carrier, class, and source boundary}

actual analytic quotient
\[
 X=(\mathbb G_m^2)^{\mathrm{an}}_K/\langle(t,2),(3,t)\rangle,
 \qquad \tau=(-\log|z_1|,-\log|z_2|).
\]
The deck transformations translate $\tau$ by $\mathbb Z^2$.
Rectangles of widths less than one give ordinary open injective
quotient charts, the compact unit polyannulus covers the quotient,
and only finitely many deck graphs meet two bounded boxes. Local
analytic gluing along these etale chart overlaps constructs $X$;
the diagonal is closed, since locally it is a finite union of closed
deck graphs. This uses the conventional analytic quotient gluing and
coherent descent of Conrad--Temkin, Lemmas 4.2.3--4.2.4, on finite
chart covers, not on the infinite covering map. Thus the carrier used
below is compact Hausdorff, good, smooth, separated, boundaryless,
and pure of dimension two. The present estimates use no algebraization
of $X$. The packet's nonalgebraization argument is retained separately
as unverified DATA, rather than counted as a completed new source audit.

On each chart put $\rho=|\tau|^2/2$, $\theta=\DD\rho$. A change
of lift changes $\rho$ by a smooth affine logarithm of a unit.
Let $\mathscr P$ be the \emph{entire} minimal continuous CLD psh
sheaf containing the ordinary smooth psh functions and closed under
local uniform limits, and define
\[
 \C=\{a\in C(X,\R):\rho+a\in\mathscr P\text{ locally}\},
 \theta_a=\theta+\DD a,\quad B(a,b)=\theta_a\wedge\theta_b,
 \MA(a)=\theta_a^2.
\]
No first-stage identity or global smooth psh approximation is assumed.
Constants, convex combinations, and finite maxima preserve $\C$:
