# Countable monotone closure with an actual analytic presentation

New theorem. On the analytic carrier, positivity datum and generated domain G reconstructed in n1, suppose u_k in G decrease pointwise and inf_k E(u_k)>-infinity. Then their ACTUAL pointwise limit u belongs to G and E(u_k) decreases to E(u). The hypothesis that the limit is already generated is unnecessary for sequences with this energy bound. No metrizability, countable point set, strictness of theta, or arbitrary-current base change is required. This is countable monotone closure, not compactness of an arbitrary sublevel net.

I give the diagonal construction explicitly; it is more than a choice of matching indices in the presentations. Choose presentations f_(k,j) in C, f_(k,j) downarrow u_k. Each continuous term is bounded on compact X; no uniform lower bound on the entire presentation is assumed. Enumerate ALL pairs (k,j) as a sequence, and denote the resulting continuous functions by h_1,h_2,... . Thus inf_m h_m=u pointwise. Every h_m dominates u. Fix epsilon_n=2^(-n), set r_n=sum_(ell>n) epsilon_ell=2^(-n), and initialize k_0=0.

The compactness lemma needed here holds even for USC outer terms: if g_k downarrow g, each g_k is USC, and a is finite continuous with g<a everywhere, then {g_k<a} is an increasing ordinary open cover of compact X. A finite subcover gives a global late index. This statement includes poles and uses strict inequality.

At stage n choose k_n>=max(n,k_(n-1)) so that

u_(k_n)<h_m+epsilon_n everywhere for all m<=n.

This is possible by the compactness lemma applied to the continuous minimum of the finitely many h_m+epsilon_n. That minimum is only a bound: it is NEVER inserted into the psh class. For n>1, u_(k_n)<=u_(k_(n-1))<=v_(n-1), so u_(k_n)<v_(n-1)+epsilon_n also holds. Apply the same lemma to the continuous presentation of u_(k_n). Select j_n such that v_n=f_(k_n,j_n) satisfies, everywhere,

v_n<h_m+epsilon_n (m<=n), and v_n<v_(n-1)+epsilon_n (n>1).

There are finitely many strict bounds at this stage, so one j_n works. Now put a_n=v_n+r_n. Constants preserve C, and

a_n-a_(n-1)<epsilon_n+r_n-r_(n-1)=0.

Thus a_n in C is decreasing. It dominates u. For fixed m and n>=m it is <h_m+epsilon_n+r_n, so its limit a is <=h_m for every m. Therefore a<=inf_m h_m=u. Combining both inequalities gives a=u pointwise, including every pole. This is a single genuine continuous analytic presentation of the original limit; it is not an abstract functional representative or an equality modulo a null set.

Let L=inf_k E(u_k)>-infinity. Since v_n>=u_(k_n), generated order preservation in n1 gives E(v_n)>=E(u_(k_n))>=L. The constant rule gives E(a_n)>=L. Hence the new presentation has finite lower energy and u belongs to G. Its upper energy is finite because its first term is continuous. The non-bottom conclusion of n1 applies, so u cannot be identically -infinity.

There is also an explicit check of the energy limit. Order gives E(u)<=E(u_k), so E(u)<=L. For any fixed continuous presentation term b_l downarrow u and eta>0, the open sets {u_k<b_l+eta} increase and cover X. The compactness lemma gives E(u_k)<=E(b_l)+2eta for large k. Taking k to infinity, then l to infinity and eta to zero, gives L<=E(u). Thus E(u_k) downarrow E(u), without circular use of continuity to prove generation.

The proof uses only compactness, USC outer terms, continuous presentations, constant stability, canonical monotone energy, and its positive mass constant rule. Its analytic applicability follows from the independent bounded-current/energy reconstruction in n1; no earlier supplied note is a premise. A naive diagonal would be wrong even on one point: f_(k,j)=0 for j<2^k and f_(k,j)=-1+1/k otherwise decreases in j to u_k=-1+1/k. The u_k decrease to -1 and have uniformly bounded energies for E(c)=2c, but f_(k,k) converges to0. The finitely many GLOBAL upper constraints above are exactly what prevents that failure.

Corollary. A countable downward directed family of members of G with a common lower energy bound has its pointwise infimum in G. Recursively choose a member below the previously chosen member and the next enumerated member. This produces a decreasing sequence coinitial in the family, to which the theorem applies. An uncountable decreasing net is covered only if it admits such a countable coinitial reduction (or another independently proved representation theorem). The construction does not provide one automatically.

Artifacts: n2.md contains the full proof; scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md integrate it with the independent bounded and generated foundations. The theorem proves an actual countable closure gate on the genuine analytic space. Separated normalized energy-sublevel compactness and full P16.7 remain unresolved.

# Ordered operator continuity and infinite convex sums

The following are new consequences of n1 and the actual countable presentation theorem n2. They impose no invariance or support restriction.

If u_k in G decrease and inf E(u_k)>-infinity, then u=inf u_k is generated by n2. The canonical energy continuity now applies with a proved actual limit. For every v in C, the coefficients of E((1-t)u_k+tv) and E(tu_k) converge by finite interpolation, and their boundary derivative identity from n1 gives integral v MA(u_k)->integral v MA(u). Density of span C and mass two give weak convergence against EVERY continuous analytic-space test. Polarization gives B(u_k,v_k)->B(u,v) if both decreasing families have finite lower energy bounds. This extends the previously conditional decreasing operator theorem to all such sequences; it does not assert general net convergence.

There is actual L1 convergence for arbitrary-support finite-full-dual measures. Let mu be positive Radon, mu(X)=2 and D=E*(mu)<infinity. The potentials u_k and u are integrable by n1, and u_1 dominates every u_k. Their decreasing differences u_k-u are nonnegative and bounded above mu-a.e. by the integrable u_1-u. Dominated convergence gives integral |u_k-u|mu->0. Moving MA moments and mixed moments follow exactly from the multivariate energy coefficients in n1, because n2 has now proved their limiting potentials generated. In particular, integral |u_k-u|MA(v_k)->0 for any second energy-bounded decreasing generated sequence v_k. These facts concern each ordered family and do not assert uniform integrability of a whole nonordered energy sublevel.

Here is a further actual analytic closure theorem. Suppose u_i in G are nonpositive, E(u_i)>=-C_i with C_i>=0, and t_i>=0 satisfy T=sum t_i<=1 and C_tot=sum t_i C_i<infinity. Omit zero coefficients, especially at poles. Define s_N=sum_(i<=N)t_i u_i and u=sum_(i>=1)t_i u_i pointwise, in R union {-infinity}. Each s_N is the finite convex combination of the u_i and zero with remaining coefficient 1-sum_(i<=N)t_i. Convexity gives s_N in G and concavity gives E(s_N)>=-sum_(i<=N)t_i C_i>=-C_tot. Because each u_i<=0, s_N decreases to the prescribed pointwise sum u. The theorem n2 supplies a single bounded continuous analytic decreasing presentation of that exact sum. Thus u in G, E(u)>=-C_tot, E(s_N) downarrow E(u), MA(s_N)->MA(u), and the sum is USC. It is not identically -infinity.

For every finite-full-dual mu as above, Tonelli and the n1 dual bound give an exact quantitative tail estimate:

integral |s_N-u|mu=sum_(i>N)t_i integral(-u_i)mu
<=D sum_(i>N)t_i+sum_(i>N)t_i C_i ->0.

All terms are nonnegative, so no undefined difference of infinite integrals occurs. On the common mu-null union of pole sets and the pole set of the sum, values of the differences may be assigned arbitrarily. This proves integrability and control for a fixed summable family, with the actual representative supplied independently by n2. It does not replace analytic potentials by an inverse Banach measure.

For completeness, the finite-dual variational objective over G equals its supremum over C: for any u in G its bounded continuous presentation satisfies E(a_j)-integral a_j mu->E(u)-integral u mu. Hence enlarging to these actual countable completions changes neither E*(mu) nor the eligible measure condition. Constants still fix the raw mass two. This is a noncircular necessary condition; none of the closure theorems proves that every such mu is MA(u).

Artifacts: n3.md, scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md contain the complete proofs. The newly constructed limits are actual analytic generated potentials. General energy-sublevel compactness, obstacle orthogonality, arbitrary-support equation existence and full uniqueness are separate remaining gates.

# All-test separation, classical recognition, and the unresolved uniqueness step

This note independently checks the entire current all-test argument and ROOT394/395. It uses the bounded and generated calculus proved in n1; the new countable closure and its consequences are n2 and n3. The published curve and classical-psh results are stated at their retained hypotheses below. No old positive verdict is a premise.

For continuous dpsh functions write $Q_T(f,h)=-\int fDD(hT)$, with the positive Hilbert pairing of n1 when $T$ is positive closed. Put $f=a-b$, $g=(a+b)/2$, $h=w-g$, and $I(a,b)=\int(a-b)[MA(b)-MA(a)]$. Bounded expansion and Green give
\[
 I(a,b)=Q_{\theta_a}(f,f)+Q_{\theta_b}(f,f)\geq0.
\]
The signed transgression is
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)-Q_{\theta_g}(f,f)
 =Q_{\theta_a}(f,h)-Q_{\theta_b}(f,h).
\]
Both sides equal $-\int fDDf\wedge DDh$ by the symmetric continuous dpsh product and $DDf=\theta_a-\theta_b$. Thus Cauchy--Schwarz in the two positive current slots gives
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)\leq I(a,b)/2+
 \sqrt{I(a,b)(Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)+Q_{\theta_b}(h,h))}.
\]

Normalize $a,b,w\leq0$ and assume $E(a),E(b),E(w)\geq-C$. The dual estimate in n1 gives $\int(-p)MA(q)\leq3C$ for any two of these weights. Since $B(q,r)\leq2MA((q+r)/2)$, concavity and the same estimate give $\int(-p)B(q,r)\leq6C$. From $|h|\leq-w+(-a-b)/2$ follow $\int|h|MA(q)\leq6C$ and $\int|h|B(q,r)\leq12C$. Expanding
\[
 Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)
 =-\int h\left[B(a,w)-(MA(a)+B(a,b))/2\right]
\]
bounds this slot by $12C+3C+6C=21C$; the other slot has the same bound. Consequently
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(a-b,a-b)\leq I(a,b)/2+\sqrt{42C I(a,b)}.
\]
This estimate tests every bounded continuous $w\in\mathcal C$, rather than just the degenerate reference current.

If generated $u,v$ have equal MA, choose any continuous decreasing presentations and subtract fixed upper constants. Their energies have a common lower bound. The four moving moments from n1 show $I(u_j,v_j)\to0$, so $Q_{\theta_w}(u_j-v_j,u_j-v_j)\to0$ for every fixed bounded test. For $u,v\in\mathcal C$ themselves the same estimate gives zero pairing. Green and Cauchy--Schwarz against compact smooth scalar tests imply $DD((u-v)\theta_w)=0$.

Here is the exact bounded divisor consequence. In a lift torus chart put $\rho_a=|x-a|^2/2$. Let $P$ be a nonzero Laurent polynomial and $\chi$ a smooth convex function, zero on $(-\infty,0]$, with $0\leq\chi'\leq1$ and $\chi(t)=t-c$ for $t\geq1$. The capped function $\psi_N=\chi(\log|P|+N)$ is ordinary smooth and psh: it is locally zero at zeros of $P$, and elsewhere is a smooth convex unit-logarithm function. Choose $0<\delta<r^2/4$ on a chart $|x_i-a_i|<r$, and a positive $\varepsilon_N$ sufficiently small to make
\[
 w_N=\max(\rho_a,\delta+\varepsilon_N\psi_N)-\rho_a
\]
zero on a tropical boundary collar. Its zero extension is in $\mathcal C$. On the fixed inner neighbourhood $\rho_a<\delta/2$ its curvature equals $\varepsilon_N DD\psi_N$.

CLDv2 Theorem16.7.3 is the Poincare--Lelong identity $DD[\log|P|]=\delta_{\operatorname{div}P}$ for a regular meromorphic function on a boundaryless pure-dimensional analytic space. The whole applied statement and immediate proof were read in LF23458--23671, including its Stokes, boundary and calibration steps. The torus chart is smooth and boundaryless and nonzero holomorphic $P$ is regular. Compact smooth top-test supports avoid the lower-dimensional divisor, so $[\psi_N-N]$ is eventually $[\log|P|-c]$ there. Hence $DD\psi_N\to\delta_{\operatorname{div}P}$. Continuous multiplier convergence CLD8.5.1, used ONLY for bounded continuous $u-v$, gives
\[
 DD((u-v)\delta_{\operatorname{div}P})=0
\]
on that fixed inner neighbourhood. This is an ambient divisor-current identity. It is not an unbounded restriction or a proof of curve harmonicity for every analytic curve.

The newer classical bridge is valid, with the following exact source scope. Gubler--Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September2025, Definition4.1 tests ALL analytic curves after ALL analytic complete field extensions. Definition3.4 uses separated pure-dimensional analytic curves over nontrivially valued fields and includes the identically-minus-infinite alternative. Theorem1.2 already proves the ordinary smooth CLD-to-classical psh implication; this is published input, not a new contribution. Theorem4.2 supplies the sheaf, convex/max and decreasing-net closure properties, analytic pullback and field-extension functoriality. The full applied units and immediate proofs were read, including the source's reductions and dependencies. Their deeper proof trees remain named foundations.

One can therefore prove the ALL-stage continuous recognition without assuming a first-stage identity. On a compact neighbourhood take classical psh $h_j$ uniformly approaching continuous $h$, and pass to a subsequence with error at most $2^{-j}$. Then $g_j=h_j+3\cdot2^{-j}$ decreases: $h_{j+1}-h_j\leq 3\cdot2^{-j-1}$, precisely the decrease of the added constants. Its limit is $h$. The source's decreasing closure proves uniform closure of the finite continuous classical sheaf. Minimality places the complete continuous CLD sheaf P in it. Hence every generated local weight $\rho+u$ is classically psh, including at poles, by the same decreasing closure. The new limits and infinite sums from n2--n3 are thus actual classically psh analytic representatives.

The source's Theorem6.4 states the affinoid Shilov maximum principle for an USC classical psh function, with arbitrary complete fields and affinoid radii: $\max_A q=\max_{\Gamma_A}q$ for affinoid $A$. Its complete immediate proof uses Theorem6.1 (local maximum), Lemma5.4 (curve connectivity) and Proposition6.3 (boundary strata); all were read. On original PDF page33 the proof calls $q$ continuous, but the closed maximum set needed there is also closed for USC $q$, the stated hypothesis. Original pages3,33,34 were viewed. This repairs that wording locally without strengthening the theorem's hypothesis.

Here are independently checked consequences, not a fixed skeleton assertion. For every point and all arbitrarily small affinoid neighbourhoods contained in a local weight chart,
\[
 q(x)=\inf_{A\ni x\text{ neighbourhood}}\max_{\Gamma_A}q.
\]
The inequality from below follows from the maximum principle. If $q(x)$ is finite, USC supplies a neighbourhood where $q<q(x)+\eta$, and an affinoid neighbourhood therein gives the reverse inequality as $\eta\to0$. If $q(x)=-\infty$, use every finite bound instead. Thus values on the union of ALL these Shilov boundaries determine pointwise weights and their order.

There is also a Hartogs upper lemma. Suppose classical psh $q_j$ are defined near compact $Q$ and $h$ is finite continuous. If $\limsup_jq_j(\xi)\leq h(\xi)$ for every Shilov point of every sufficiently small affinoid neighbourhood, then eventually $q_j\leq h+\eta$ on $Q$. Choose a finite affinoid cover of $Q$ on each member of which the oscillation of $h$ is less than $\eta/3$. Each finite Shilov boundary has all $q_j(\xi)\leq h(\xi)+\eta/3$ eventually; one late index works for the finite cover. The maximum principle then gives the assertion (with room in the constants). The same proof works for a net using finite directed upper bounds. This is upper control only.

Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, 8 November2018, Theorem4.7, states that a continuous function on an open subset of a smooth PROPER algebraic curve over a complete ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED NONTRIVIALLY VALUED field is Thuillier-subharmonic if and only if its CLD Hessian current is positive. Properness is the standing hypothesis of Section4, explicitly checked at LF793--810. Its full immediate six-step proof was read, together with Definitions2.4,3.18 and the necessary smooth recognition/pullback results3.20--21 and approximation4.6. ROOT394's minimality bridge on those curve tests is valid at exactly these hypotheses. GR's all-extension definition avoids limiting classical recognition to these algebraic tests. Neither theorem transports the surface energy/current identity to a larger field or proves that ambient divisor tests recover all tests on an arbitrary curve.

The retained ROOT394 bridge itself has a short independent proof. Our local weight charts are open torus analytifications, so smooth ambient psh weights pull back to smooth psh weights on the stated algebraic curve tests by Wanner3.21, including after the stated field extension. Among finite continuous ambient functions, those whose pullbacks have positive curve Hessian currents form a sheaf closed under local uniform limits: uniform pullback convergence and continuous coefficient/current differentiation give weak Hessian convergence, and positivity is closed. This sheaf contains the smooth psh weights, so minimality contains every stage of P. Wanner4.7 recognizes these CONTINUOUS curve pullbacks. The decreasing extended-weight conclusion follows from the GR decreasing closure at those same curve tests, including the identically-minus-infinite case. This uses functorial pullback of functions and smooth tropicalizations, not a base-change formula for surface products or energy.

The separation and compactness gates therefore remain. We have not shown that $DD((u-v)\delta_{\operatorname{div}P})=0$ implies that every curve pullback of $u-v$ is harmonic, or that zero pairings determine an actual generated difference pointwise modulo constants. Such an argument must prove the divisor restriction, test-extension and any base-change steps; unbounded differences additionally need divisor integrability and null-set removability. Shilov reconstruction would identify weights if equality on ALL its boundary values were proved, but equal MA supplies no such equality yet. Upper boundary control supplies neither lower control nor uniform integrability of a general energy sublevel. These are precise unresolved steps, not claimed counterexamples to P16.7.

\begin{abstract}
We independently reconstruct the current generated-current calculus on a proper
nonalgebraizable analytic surface and prove a new countable closure theorem.
Every decreasing sequence of actual generated potentials with a common lower
energy bound has a single continuous decreasing presentation of its actual
pointwise limit. Energy continuity, ordered Monge--Ampere convergence and
summable convex-series closure follow. Full energy-sublevel compactness,
arbitrary-measure existence and pointwise uniqueness remain unresolved.
This is a scoped unverified draft, not a solution of the original P16.7.
\end{abstract}

\section*{Carrier, domain and precise new statement}
Retain $K=\mathbf C((s))$, $|s|=e^{-1/8}$, $t=s^8$, and
\[
 X=(\mathbf G_m^2)^{\mathrm{an}}/\langle(t,2),(3,t)\rangle,
 \qquad x_i=-\log|z_i|,\quad \rho=|x|^2/2,\quad \theta=\DD\rho.
\]
Affine changes of $\rho$ along periods give a global smooth closed curvature
datum of raw top mass $M=2$. The independent geometric argument and its exact
conventional foundations appear in the reconstruction below. Let $\C$ be the
continuous weights $a$ on $X$ for which $\rho+a$ belongs locally to the full
minimal continuous CLD psh sheaf. This uses all uniform-closure stages.
The actual positive bounded products are
\[
 B(a,b)=\theta\wedge\theta_b+\DD(a\theta_b),\qquad
 \theta_b=\theta+\DD[b],\qquad \MA(a)=B(a,a).
\]
The energy is the canonical cubic
\[
 E(a)=\frac13\int_X a\,[\MA(0)+B(a,0)+\MA(a)].
\]
It is monotone, concave, and satisfies $E(a+c)=E(a)+Mc$.
Define $\G$ to be the \emph{actual pointwise} limits $a_j\downarrow u$,
$a_j\in\C$, with $\inf_j E(a_j)>-\infty$. The reconstruction proves that
$E(u)=\lim_jE(a_j)$ is independent of every such presentation, preserves
order, and that $u$ is USC and is not identically $-\infty$.
Neither this definition nor the theorem assumes intrinsic recognition of
every unbounded psh function.

\begin{lemma}[Strict compact dominance]
Let $X$ be compact, let USC $g_k$ decrease pointwise to $g$, and let $a$ be
finite continuous with $g<a$ everywhere. Then $g_k<a$ everywhere for all
sufficiently large $k$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The ordinary open sets $\{g_k<a\}$ increase and cover $X$.
A finite subcover has a largest index. The proof includes points where
$g=-\infty$ and does not require metrizability.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Actual countable monotone closure]
If $u_k\in\G$ decrease pointwise and $L=\inf_kE(u_k)>-\infty$, their actual
pointwise infimum $u$ belongs to $\G$, and $E(u_k)\downarrow E(u)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Choose $f_{k,j}\in\C$ decreasing in $j$ to $u_k$ and enumerate every pair
$(k,j)$ as continuous functions $h_1,h_2,\ldots$. Then
$\inf_mh_m=\inf_ku_k=u$ at every point. Put
\[
 \epsilon_n=2^{-n},\qquad r_n=\sum_{\ell>n}\epsilon_\ell=2^{-n}.
\]
Each continuous term is bounded on compact $X$; no uniform lower bound on
the entire presentation is assumed. Initialize $k_0=0$.
Inductively choose $k_n\geq\max(n,k_{n-1})$ with
$u_{k_n}<h_m+\epsilon_n$ on all of $X$ for $m\leq n$.
The lemma applies to the finite continuous minimum of these bounds.
That minimum is used only as a bound, never as a psh potential.
For $n>1$, also $u_{k_n}\leq u_{k_{n-1}}\leq v_{n-1}$, where the preceding
stage has selected $v_{n-1}$. Apply the lemma to the presentation of $u_{k_n}$
to choose $j_n$ such that $v_n=f_{k_n,j_n}$ obeys
\[
 v_n<h_m+\epsilon_n\ (m\leq n),\qquad
 v_n<v_{n-1}+\epsilon_n\ (n>1).
\]
All bounds are strict and finite continuous, so a single index works.
Let $a_n=v_n+r_n$. Constant stability gives $a_n\in\C$, and
\[
 a_n-a_{n-1}<\epsilon_n+r_n-r_{n-1}=0\quad(n>1).
\]
Each $a_n\geq u$. Its decreasing limit $a$ satisfies $a\leq h_m$ for every
$m$, since $a_n<h_m+\epsilon_n+r_n$ for $n\geq m$.
Hence $a=u$ pointwise, including all poles.
Order preservation and the constant rule give
$E(a_n)\geq E(u_{k_n})\geq L$. This proves $u\in\G$ without presupposing
generation of the limit.

Order gives $E(u)\leq L$. For a presentation $b_\ell\downarrow u$ and any
$\eta>0$, the lemma gives $u_k<b_\ell+\eta$ globally eventually.
Thus $L\leq E(b_\ell)+M\eta$. Let $\ell\to\infty$ and then
$\eta\to0$ to obtain $L\leq E(u)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Countable directed infima]
A countable downward directed family in $\G$ with a common lower energy
bound has its actual pointwise infimum in $\G$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Enumerate the family and recursively choose a member below both the previous
choice and the next enumerated member. The resulting decreasing sequence is
coinitial. Apply the theorem. No uncountable coinitiality assertion follows.
\end{proof}

\section*{Actual operator and measure consequences}
The reconstructed generated operator is a limit of genuine bounded analytic
products. For $a_j\downarrow u$ and a bounded test $v\in\C$, the identity
\[
 \int_Xv\,\MA(a_j)
 =\left.\frac{d}{dt}E((1-t)a_j+tv)\right|_{t=0}
  +\left.\frac{d}{dt}E(ta_j)\right|_{t=1}
\]
and finite interpolation of cubic coefficients prove presentation independence.
The actual test lattice $\operatorname{span}\C$ is dense in $C(X)$, so the
limit is a positive Radon measure of raw mass two on the entire analytic space.
The reconstruction supplies mixed polarization, finite dual, moving moments,
comparison and exact contact-excluding locality before the new theorem is used.

\begin{corollary}[Ordered continuity without prior generation]
For the sequences in the theorem, $\MA(u_k)\to\MA(u)$ weakly against all
of $C(X)$. If also $v_k\downarrow v$ has a finite lower energy bound, then
$B(u_k,v_k)\to B(u,v)$ and
$\int|u_k-u|\MA(v_k)\to0$.
For every positive Radon $\mu$ of mass two and finite full bounded dual
\[
 E^*(\mu)=\sup_{a\in\C}\left(E(a)-\int a\,d\mu\right),
\]
one has $\int|u_k-u|\,d\mu\to0$, without any support restriction.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The theorem has now supplied actual generated limits. Cubic interpolation at
every finite convex combination gives the coefficient limits in the displayed
test identity; density and common mass give all-continuous-test convergence.
Polarization and the multivariate energy moments give the mixed and moving
conclusions, with the full moment proof recorded below. Finite dual makes
$u_1$ and $u$ integrable. Off their null pole sets,
$0\leq u_k-u\leq u_1-u\in L^1(\mu)$, so dominated convergence proves the
last conclusion. This is an ordered-family statement, not uniform
integrability of a nonordered energy sublevel.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Summable nonpositive convex series]
Let $u_i\in\G$, $u_i\leq0$, $E(u_i)\geq-C_i$, $C_i\geq0$, and let
$t_i\geq0$, $\sum_i t_i\leq1$, $\sum_it_iC_i<\infty$. Omitting zero
terms, the actual pointwise sum $u=\sum_it_iu_i$ belongs to $\G$ and
\[
 E(u)\geq-\sum_it_iC_i,\qquad
 E(s_N)\downarrow E(u),\qquad\MA(s_N)\to\MA(u),
 \quad s_N=\sum_{i\leq N}t_iu_i.
\]
For every finite-full-dual $\mu$ of mass two, with $D=E^*(\mu)$,
\[
 \int|s_N-u|\,d\mu
 \leq D\sum_{i>N}t_i+\sum_{i>N}t_iC_i\longrightarrow0.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The remaining coefficient at zero makes $s_N$ a finite convex combination.
Concavity gives $E(s_N)\geq-\sum_{i\leq N}t_iC_i$. Nonpositivity gives
$s_N\downarrow u$, so the countable closure theorem and ordered continuity
apply to the actual sum. The dual bound
$\int(-u_i)\,d\mu\leq D-E(u_i)\leq D+C_i$ and Tonelli give the tail
estimate. The countable union of pole sets and the pole set of $u$ are
$\mu$-null, so differences may be assigned arbitrary values there.
\end{proof}

\section*{Scope of the unchanged problem}
The new theorem addresses countable actual representation. It proves no
separated normalized energy-sublevel compactness, unrestricted obstacle
orthogonality, arbitrary-support variational existence or full pointwise
uniqueness. Equal MA gives vanishing all-test bounded gradients; for bounded
continuous differences it gives Laurent divisor-current identities.
The full classical-psh and Shilov source application is checked below.
It does not license a field-change energy identity or an unbounded divisor
restriction. All original P16.7 gates remain as stated in the residual record.
The following complete reconstruction and ledger are part of this standalone
paper; neither historical verdicts nor executable supplied programs are premises.

\section*{Countable monotone closure with an actual analytic presentation}

New theorem. On the analytic carrier, positivity datum and generated domain G reconstructed in n1, suppose u\_k in G decrease pointwise and inf\_k E(u\_k)>-infinity. Then their ACTUAL pointwise limit u belongs to G and E(u\_k) decreases to E(u). The hypothesis that the limit is already generated is unnecessary for sequences with this energy bound. No metrizability, countable point set, strictness of theta, or arbitrary-current base change is required. This is countable monotone closure, not compactness of an arbitrary sublevel net.

I give the diagonal construction explicitly; it is more than a choice of matching indices in the presentations. Choose presentations f\_(k,j) in C, f\_(k,j) downarrow u\_k. Each continuous term is bounded on compact X; no uniform lower bound on the entire presentation is assumed. Enumerate ALL pairs (k,j) as a sequence, and denote the resulting continuous functions by h\_1,h\_2,... . Thus inf\_m h\_m=u pointwise. Every h\_m dominates u. Fix epsilon\_n=2\textasciicircum{}(-n), set r\_n=sum\_(ell>n) epsilon\_ell=2\textasciicircum{}(-n), and initialize k\_0=0.

The compactness lemma needed here holds even for USC outer terms: if g\_k downarrow g, each g\_k is USC, and a is finite continuous with g<a everywhere, then \{g\_k<a\} is an increasing ordinary open cover of compact X. A finite subcover gives a global late index. This statement includes poles and uses strict inequality.

At stage n choose k\_n>=max(n,k\_(n-1)) so that

u\_(k\_n)<h\_m+epsilon\_n everywhere for all m<=n.

This is possible by the compactness lemma applied to the continuous minimum of the finitely many h\_m+epsilon\_n. That minimum is only a bound: it is NEVER inserted into the psh class. For n>1, u\_(k\_n)<=u\_(k\_(n-1))<=v\_(n-1), so u\_(k\_n)<v\_(n-1)+epsilon\_n also holds. Apply the same lemma to the continuous presentation of u\_(k\_n). Select j\_n such that v\_n=f\_(k\_n,j\_n) satisfies, everywhere,

v\_n<h\_m+epsilon\_n (m<=n), and v\_n<v\_(n-1)+epsilon\_n (n>1).

There are finitely many strict bounds at this stage, so one j\_n works. Now put a\_n=v\_n+r\_n. Constants preserve C, and

a\_n-a\_(n-1)<epsilon\_n+r\_n-r\_(n-1)=0.

Thus a\_n in C is decreasing. It dominates u. For fixed m and n>=m it is <h\_m+epsilon\_n+r\_n, so its limit a is <=h\_m for every m. Therefore a<=inf\_m h\_m=u. Combining both inequalities gives a=u pointwise, including every pole. This is a single genuine continuous analytic presentation of the original limit; it is not an abstract functional representative or an equality modulo a null set.

Let L=inf\_k E(u\_k)>-infinity. Since v\_n>=u\_(k\_n), generated order preservation in n1 gives E(v\_n)>=E(u\_(k\_n))>=L. The constant rule gives E(a\_n)>=L. Hence the new presentation has finite lower energy and u belongs to G. Its upper energy is finite because its first term is continuous. The non-bottom conclusion of n1 applies, so u cannot be identically -infinity.

There is also an explicit check of the energy limit. Order gives E(u)<=E(u\_k), so E(u)<=L. For any fixed continuous presentation term b\_l downarrow u and eta>0, the open sets \{u\_k<b\_l+eta\} increase and cover X. The compactness lemma gives E(u\_k)<=E(b\_l)+2eta for large k. Taking k to infinity, then l to infinity and eta to zero, gives L<=E(u). Thus E(u\_k) downarrow E(u), without circular use of continuity to prove generation.

The proof uses only compactness, USC outer terms, continuous presentations, constant stability, canonical monotone energy, and its positive mass constant rule. Its analytic applicability follows from the independent bounded-current/energy reconstruction in n1; no earlier supplied note is a premise. A naive diagonal would be wrong even on one point: f\_(k,j)=0 for j<2\textasciicircum{}k and f\_(k,j)=-1+1/k otherwise decreases in j to u\_k=-1+1/k. The u\_k decrease to -1 and have uniformly bounded energies for E(c)=2c, but f\_(k,k) converges to0. The finitely many GLOBAL upper constraints above are exactly what prevents that failure.

Corollary. A countable downward directed family of members of G with a common lower energy bound has its pointwise infimum in G. Recursively choose a member below the previously chosen member and the next enumerated member. This produces a decreasing sequence coinitial in the family, to which the theorem applies. An uncountable decreasing net is covered only if it admits such a countable coinitial reduction (or another independently proved representation theorem). The construction does not provide one automatically.

\section*{Ordered operator continuity and infinite convex sums}

The following are new consequences of n1 and the actual countable presentation theorem n2. They impose no invariance or support restriction.

If u\_k in G decrease and inf E(u\_k)>-infinity, then u=inf u\_k is generated by n2. The canonical energy continuity now applies with a proved actual limit. For every v in C, the coefficients of E((1-t)u\_k+tv) and E(tu\_k) converge by finite interpolation, and their boundary derivative identity from n1 gives integral v MA(u\_k)->integral v MA(u). Density of span C and mass two give weak convergence against EVERY continuous analytic-space test. Polarization gives B(u\_k,v\_k)->B(u,v) if both decreasing families have finite lower energy bounds. This extends the previously conditional decreasing operator theorem to all such sequences; it does not assert general net convergence.

There is actual L1 convergence for arbitrary-support finite-full-dual measures. Let mu be positive Radon, mu(X)=2 and D=E*(mu)<infinity. The potentials u\_k and u are integrable by n1, and u\_1 dominates every u\_k. Their decreasing differences u\_k-u are nonnegative and bounded above mu-a.e. by the integrable u\_1-u. Dominated convergence gives integral |u\_k-u|mu->0. Moving MA moments and mixed moments follow exactly from the multivariate energy coefficients in n1, because n2 has now proved their limiting potentials generated. In particular, integral |u\_k-u|MA(v\_k)->0 for any second energy-bounded decreasing generated sequence v\_k. These facts concern each ordered family and do not assert uniform integrability of a whole nonordered energy sublevel.

Here is a further actual analytic closure theorem. Suppose u\_i in G are nonpositive, E(u\_i)>=-C\_i with C\_i>=0, and t\_i>=0 satisfy T=sum t\_i<=1 and C\_tot=sum t\_i C\_i<infinity. Omit zero coefficients, especially at poles. Define s\_N=sum\_(i<=N)t\_i u\_i and u=sum\_(i>=1)t\_i u\_i pointwise, in R union \{-infinity\}. Each s\_N is the finite convex combination of the u\_i and zero with remaining coefficient 1-sum\_(i<=N)t\_i. Convexity gives s\_N in G and concavity gives E(s\_N)>=-sum\_(i<=N)t\_i C\_i>=-C\_tot. Because each u\_i<=0, s\_N decreases to the prescribed pointwise sum u. The theorem n2 supplies a single bounded continuous analytic decreasing presentation of that exact sum. Thus u in G, E(u)>=-C\_tot, E(s\_N) downarrow E(u), MA(s\_N)->MA(u), and the sum is USC. It is not identically -infinity.

For every finite-full-dual mu as above, Tonelli and the n1 dual bound give an exact quantitative tail estimate:

integral |s\_N-u|mu=sum\_(i>N)t\_i integral(-u\_i)mu
<=D sum\_(i>N)t\_i+sum\_(i>N)t\_i C\_i ->0.

All terms are nonnegative, so no undefined difference of infinite integrals occurs. On the common mu-null union of pole sets and the pole set of the sum, values of the differences may be assigned arbitrarily. This proves integrability and control for a fixed summable family, with the actual representative supplied independently by n2. It does not replace analytic potentials by an inverse Banach measure.

For completeness, the finite-dual variational objective over G equals its supremum over C: for any u in G its bounded continuous presentation satisfies E(a\_j)-integral a\_j mu->E(u)-integral u mu. Hence enlarging to these actual countable completions changes neither E*(mu) nor the eligible measure condition. Constants still fix the raw mass two. This is a noncircular necessary condition; none of the closure theorems proves that every such mu is MA(u).

\section*{All-test separation, classical recognition, and the unresolved uniqueness step}

This note independently checks the entire current all-test argument and ROOT394/395. It uses the bounded and generated calculus proved in n1; the new countable closure and its consequences are n2 and n3. The published curve and classical-psh results are stated at their retained hypotheses below. No old positive verdict is a premise.

For continuous dpsh functions write $Q_T(f,h)=-\int fDD(hT)$, with the positive Hilbert pairing of n1 when $T$ is positive closed. Put $f=a-b$, $g=(a+b)/2$, $h=w-g$, and $I(a,b)=\int(a-b)[MA(b)-MA(a)]$. Bounded expansion and Green give
\[
 I(a,b)=Q_{\theta_a}(f,f)+Q_{\theta_b}(f,f)\geq0.
\]
The signed transgression is
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)-Q_{\theta_g}(f,f)
 =Q_{\theta_a}(f,h)-Q_{\theta_b}(f,h).
\]
Both sides equal $-\int fDDf\wedge DDh$ by the symmetric continuous dpsh product and $DDf=\theta_a-\theta_b$. Thus Cauchy--Schwarz in the two positive current slots gives
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)\leq I(a,b)/2+
 \sqrt{I(a,b)(Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)+Q_{\theta_b}(h,h))}.
\]

Normalize $a,b,w\leq0$ and assume $E(a),E(b),E(w)\geq-C$. The dual estimate in n1 gives $\int(-p)MA(q)\leq3C$ for any two of these weights. Since $B(q,r)\leq2MA((q+r)/2)$, concavity and the same estimate give $\int(-p)B(q,r)\leq6C$. From $|h|\leq-w+(-a-b)/2$ follow $\int|h|MA(q)\leq6C$ and $\int|h|B(q,r)\leq12C$. Expanding
\[
 Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)
 =-\int h\left[B(a,w)-(MA(a)+B(a,b))/2\right]
\]
bounds this slot by $12C+3C+6C=21C$; the other slot has the same bound. Consequently
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(a-b,a-b)\leq I(a,b)/2+\sqrt{42C I(a,b)}.
\]
This estimate tests every bounded continuous $w\in\mathcal C$, rather than just the degenerate reference current.

If generated $u,v$ have equal MA, choose any continuous decreasing presentations and subtract fixed upper constants. Their energies have a common lower bound. The four moving moments from n1 show $I(u_j,v_j)\to0$, so $Q_{\theta_w}(u_j-v_j,u_j-v_j)\to0$ for every fixed bounded test. For $u,v\in\mathcal C$ themselves the same estimate gives zero pairing. Green and Cauchy--Schwarz against compact smooth scalar tests imply $DD((u-v)\theta_w)=0$.

Here is the exact bounded divisor consequence. In a lift torus chart put $\rho_a=|x-a|^2/2$. Let $P$ be a nonzero Laurent polynomial and $\chi$ a smooth convex function, zero on $(-\infty,0]$, with $0\leq\chi'\leq1$ and $\chi(t)=t-c$ for $t\geq1$. The capped function $\psi_N=\chi(\log|P|+N)$ is ordinary smooth and psh: it is locally zero at zeros of $P$, and elsewhere is a smooth convex unit-logarithm function. Choose $0<\delta<r^2/4$ on a chart $|x_i-a_i|<r$, and a positive $\varepsilon_N$ sufficiently small to make
\[
 w_N=\max(\rho_a,\delta+\varepsilon_N\psi_N)-\rho_a
\]
zero on a tropical boundary collar. Its zero extension is in $\mathcal C$. On the fixed inner neighbourhood $\rho_a<\delta/2$ its curvature equals $\varepsilon_N DD\psi_N$.

CLDv2 Theorem16.7.3 is the Poincare--Lelong identity $DD[\log|P|]=\delta_{\operatorname{div}P}$ for a regular meromorphic function on a boundaryless pure-dimensional analytic space. The whole applied statement and immediate proof were read in LF23458--23671, including its Stokes, boundary and calibration steps. The torus chart is smooth and boundaryless and nonzero holomorphic $P$ is regular. Compact smooth top-test supports avoid the lower-dimensional divisor, so $[\psi_N-N]$ is eventually $[\log|P|-c]$ there. Hence $DD\psi_N\to\delta_{\operatorname{div}P}$. Continuous multiplier convergence CLD8.5.1, used ONLY for bounded continuous $u-v$, gives
\[
 DD((u-v)\delta_{\operatorname{div}P})=0
\]
on that fixed inner neighbourhood. This is an ambient divisor-current identity. It is not an unbounded restriction or a proof of curve harmonicity for every analytic curve.

The newer classical bridge is valid, with the following exact source scope. Gubler--Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September2025, Definition4.1 tests ALL analytic curves after ALL analytic complete field extensions. Definition3.4 uses separated pure-dimensional analytic curves over nontrivially valued fields and includes the identically-minus-infinite alternative. Theorem1.2 already proves the ordinary smooth CLD-to-classical psh implication; this is published input, not a new contribution. Theorem4.2 supplies the sheaf, convex/max and decreasing-net closure properties, analytic pullback and field-extension functoriality. The full applied units and immediate proofs were read, including the source's reductions and dependencies. Their deeper proof trees remain named foundations.

One can therefore prove the ALL-stage continuous recognition without assuming a first-stage identity. On a compact neighbourhood take classical psh $h_j$ uniformly approaching continuous $h$, and pass to a subsequence with error at most $2^{-j}$. Then $g_j=h_j+3\cdot2^{-j}$ decreases: $h_{j+1}-h_j\leq 3\cdot2^{-j-1}$, precisely the decrease of the added constants. Its limit is $h$. The source's decreasing closure proves uniform closure of the finite continuous classical sheaf. Minimality places the complete continuous CLD sheaf P in it. Hence every generated local weight $\rho+u$ is classically psh, including at poles, by the same decreasing closure. The source's Theorem6.4 states the affinoid Shilov maximum principle for an USC classical psh function, with arbitrary complete fields and affinoid radii: $\max_A q=\max_{\Gamma_A}q$ for affinoid $A$. Its complete immediate proof uses Theorem6.1 (local maximum), Lemma5.4 (curve connectivity) and Proposition6.3 (boundary strata); all were read. On original PDF page33 the proof calls $q$ continuous, but the closed maximum set needed there is also closed for USC $q$, the stated hypothesis. Original pages3,33,34 were viewed. This repairs that wording locally without strengthening the theorem's hypothesis.

Here are independently checked consequences, not a fixed skeleton assertion. For every point and all arbitrarily small affinoid neighbourhoods contained in a local weight chart,
\[
 q(x)=\inf_{A\ni x\text{ neighbourhood}}\max_{\Gamma_A}q.
\]
The inequality from below follows from the maximum principle. If $q(x)$ is finite, USC supplies a neighbourhood where $q<q(x)+\eta$, and an affinoid neighbourhood therein gives the reverse inequality as $\eta\to0$. If $q(x)=-\infty$, use every finite bound instead. Thus values on the union of ALL these Shilov boundaries determine pointwise weights and their order.

There is also a Hartogs upper lemma. Suppose classical psh $q_j$ are defined near compact $Q$ and $h$ is finite continuous. If $\limsup_jq_j(\xi)\leq h(\xi)$ for every Shilov point of every sufficiently small affinoid neighbourhood, then eventually $q_j\leq h+\eta$ on $Q$. Choose a finite affinoid cover of $Q$ on each member of which the oscillation of $h$ is less than $\eta/3$. Each finite Shilov boundary has all $q_j(\xi)\leq h(\xi)+\eta/3$ eventually; one late index works for the finite cover. The maximum principle then gives the assertion (with room in the constants). The same proof works for a net using finite directed upper bounds. This is upper control only.

Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, 8 November2018, Theorem4.7, states that a continuous function on an open subset of a smooth PROPER algebraic curve over a complete ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED NONTRIVIALLY VALUED field is Thuillier-subharmonic if and only if its CLD Hessian current is positive. Properness is the standing hypothesis of Section4, explicitly checked at LF793--810. Neither theorem transports the surface energy/current identity to a larger field or proves that ambient divisor tests recover all tests on an arbitrary curve.

The retained ROOT394 bridge itself has a short independent proof. Our local weight charts are open torus analytifications, so smooth ambient psh weights pull back to smooth psh weights on the stated algebraic curve tests by Wanner3.21, including after the stated field extension. Among finite continuous ambient functions, those whose pullbacks have positive curve Hessian currents form a sheaf closed under local uniform limits: uniform pullback convergence and continuous coefficient/current differentiation give weak Hessian convergence, and positivity is closed. The separation and compactness gates therefore remain. \title{Local analytic divisor tests for bounded solution differences\\and the remaining pluriharmonic recognition gate}
\author{Working paper; independent review pending}
\date{9 October 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
On the specified compact analytic torus quotient, equality of bounded
continuous Monge--Ampere measures forces the difference to be harmonic
against every local principal analytic divisor current. We give the
bounded Green argument, globally glued capped-log tests, and the passage
from Laurent polynomials to arbitrary local holomorphic functions by
rational-domain approximation. The last passage uses convergence of
positive currents and continuous multiplication, without assuming that
a continuously weighted closed current is closed. Separately, the
classical pluriharmonic maximum principle gives a precise sufficient
recognition criterion for uniqueness. Recognition of the solution
difference by all curve tests, unbounded restriction, compactness of
finite-energy sublevels, and general equation existence remain open.
\end{abstract}

\section{Carrier, domain, and exact foundations}
Put $K=\mathbb C((s))$, $|s|=e^{-1/8}$, and let
\[
 X=((\mathbb G_m)^2)^{\mathrm{an}}/
 \langle(s^8,2),(3,s^8)\rangle,
 \qquad x_i=-\log|z_i|,
 \quad \rho=\tfrac12|x|^2,
 \quad\theta=\DD\rho.
\]
We retain the compact, connected, smooth, good, boundaryless analytic
quotient and its ordinary injective torus-chart atlas as geometric
foundations. Tropical translation by the periods is $\mathbb Z^2$;
rectangles of coordinate width less than one give injective charts.
The local reference potentials differ by affine functions of unit
logarithms, so their Hessians glue. Quotient existence, separatedness,
properness and nonalgebraization are separate geometric statements;
the present theorem does not reestablish their entire proof trees.

Let $\mathscr P$ be the minimal sheaf of finite continuous functions
containing ordinary smooth CLD psh functions and closed under locally
uniform limits. Let
\[
 \mathcal C=\{u\in C(X,\mathbb R):\rho+u\in\mathscr P
                         \text{ on every chart}\}.
\]
Here every continuous-sheaf stage is retained. Convex combinations and
finite maxima preserve this class: prove the assertions for smooth
weights by convexity and smooth convex soft maxima, then use minimality
and uniform closure successively in the two slots.

The immediately applied CLD v2 foundations are Definition8.1.7 and
Lemma8.1.8; Lemmas8.5.1,8.5.3,8.5.5; the symmetric recursive continuous
products in8.7.1,8.7.2,8.7.4; multilinear continuous dpsh calculus and
smooth null changes in8.8.4--5; scalar Radon recognition and
smooth-coefficient measures in7.2.8,7.2.11--12; compact-support
Green/Stokes in5.11.1; calibrated integration15.7.1; and
Poincare--Lelong16.7.3~\cite{CLD}.
They give positive closed products, local uniform continuity, and the
following multiplier rule: if positive currents $T_j$ converge weakly
to $T$ and continuous coefficients converge locally uniformly, their
products converge weakly. We use only scalar and surface $(1,1)$
positivity; no higher-degree strong-cone order unit is assumed.
Smooth cutoffs and the underlying calibrated integration are ordinary
published foundations. The whole immediate applied source units were
read; deeper recursive proofs are not all newly audited.

We also use the defining Tate-algebra presentation of a rational domain
and the density of finite polynomials in a completed Tate algebra;
the latter follows directly by truncating its convergent series.
The ordinary presentation and its universal-property argument are
Van der Put2.1--2.2~\cite{VdP}; the strict presentation is also stated
in Papikian3.4--3.5~\cite{Pap}.
This includes generalized polyannulus radii. Rational domains form a
compact neighborhood basis inside a good affinoid torus chart.
These are ordinary affinoid foundations, not a claimed approximation
by polynomials on an arbitrary open set without shrinking.

\section{Bounded Green calculus at all continuous stages}
Fix a positive closed $(1,1)$ current $T$. Complete compact smooth
$(1,0)$ forms modulo the null space of the positive pairing
$\int a\wedge Jb\wedge T$. With a nonnegative compact smooth cutoff
$\chi$, write the local gradient pairing as $Q_{T,\chi}$.
Let $\mathscr H_T$ consist of continuous functions locally approximable
uniformly by smooth functions whose gradients converge strongly in
these cutoff seminorms.

Gradients are unique: if smooth $f_j\to0$ uniformly and their gradients
converge strongly to $a$, then, for each compact smooth form $b$,
closedness of $T$ gives
\[
 \int d'f_j\wedge Jb\wedge T
 =-\int f_jd'(Jb)\wedge T\longrightarrow0.
\]
The right side pairs $f_j$ with a finite signed measure. Smooth forms
are dense in the completion, so $a=0$. Smaller patches and cutoffs
give the same local assertion. Smooth partitions patch approximants:
the gradient of $\sum\chi_i f_{i,j}$ splits into
$\sum\chi_i d'f_{i,j}+\sum f_{i,j}d'\chi_i$, with both sums strongly
convergent. Bounded continuous multiplication of forms follows by
scalar smooth approximation and the norm bound. Products and cutoffs
of functions in $\mathscr H_T$ therefore have the usual gradient rule.

If $f\in\mathscr H_T$ and $L_Tf=\DD(fT)$ is signed Radon, smooth
approximation first in $f$, then uniformly and strongly in a compactly
supported $g\in\mathscr H_T$, proves
\[
 \int gL_Tf=-Q_T(f,g).
\]
In particular the product rule yields
\[
 Q_{T,\chi}(w,w)
 =\tfrac12\int w^2\DD\chi\wedge T-\int\chi w L_Tw.
\]
The sheaf of $f\in\mathscr H_T$ with $L_Tf\ge0$ contains smooth psh
functions and is uniformly closed. Indeed choose nested cutoffs
$\chi,\eta$, with $\eta=1$ near $\operatorname{supp}\chi$, and a common
bound $|f_j|\le B$ on the whole support of $\eta$. For
$\epsilon=\|f_j-f_k\|$ there, positivity and integration by parts give
\[
 0\le Q_{T,\chi}(f_j-f_k,f_j-f_k)
 \le\tfrac{\epsilon^2}{2}\|\DD\chi\wedge T\|_{TV}
 +2B\epsilon\|\chi\|_\infty\|\DD\eta\wedge T\|_{TV}.
\]
To obtain smooth approximants to the limit on a smaller patch, choose
an approximant to each $f_j$ with uniform and gradient error at most
$1/j$ for a cutoff equal to one on that patch. The displayed estimate
proves strong convergence. Positivity survives distributional limits.
Minimality now puts all of $\mathscr P$ in this sheaf. Its vector span
contains continuous dpsh functions. Finite patching on compact $X$
proves the global formula
\[
 \int f\DD(gT)=\int g\DD(fT)=-Q_T(f,g),
 \qquad Q_T(f,f)\ge0,
\]
and Cauchy--Schwarz for continuous dpsh functions. This argument uses
positive Laplacians and signed measures, not arbitrary continuous
multiplier closedness.

For $u\in\mathcal C$ write $\theta_u=\theta+\DD u$ and
$B(u,v)=\theta_u\wedge\theta_v$ for the actual recursive local
products, glued through the smooth null potential changes.
Set $\MA(u)=B(u,u)$. Every mixed measure has the same finite mass
$M=\int\theta^2=2$; Green/Stokes annihilates the exact terms.

\section{An elementary bounded all-test estimate}
Let $a,b,w\in\mathcal C$, set $f=a-b$, $g=(a+b)/2$, $h=w-g$, and
\[
 I(a,b)=\int(a-b)(\MA(b)-\MA(a)).
\]
The bounded product expansion gives
\[
 I=Q_{\theta_a}(f,f)+Q_{\theta_b}(f,f)\ge0.
\]
Multilinearity and Green give the signed identity
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)-Q_{\theta_g}(f,f)
 =Q_{\theta_a}(f,h)-Q_{\theta_b}(f,h).
\]
Indeed both sides are $-\int f\DD f\wedge\DD h$.
Thus Cauchy--Schwarz implies
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)\le I/2+
 \sqrt{I\bigl(Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)+Q_{\theta_b}(h,h)\bigr)}.
\]
For an explicit bounded version choose $B_0$ with
$|a|,|b|,|w|\le B_0$. Then $|h|\le2B_0$, and
\[
 Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)
 =-\int h\,[B(a,w)-(\MA(a)+B(a,b))/2]
 \le4MB_0.
\]
The same holds in the $b$ slot, since every positive measure in the
brackets has mass $M$. Consequently
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(a-b,a-b)\le I/2+\sqrt{8MB_0I}.
\]
This estimate is sufficient here; it claims no uniform sup-norm bound
for unbounded generated presentations.

\begin{lemma}\label{annihilate}
If $u,v\in\mathcal C$ satisfy $\MA(u)=\MA(v)$ and $d=u-v$, then
$\DD(d\theta_w)=0$ for every $w\in\mathcal C$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Equality of the measures gives $I(u,v)=0$. The estimate gives
$Q_{\theta_w}(d,d)=0$. Cauchy--Schwarz with compact smooth scalar
tests and the Green identity show that every test pairing of
$\DD(d\theta_w)$ vanishes. The difference is bounded and continuous.
\end{proof}

\section{Laurent divisor currents from glued smooth caps}
Take a nonzero Laurent polynomial $A$. At a point of its zero locus
choose an injective chart $|x_i-a_i|<r<1/2$, and put
$\rho_a=|x-a|^2/2$. Choose a smooth convex $\chi$ with
$\chi=0$ on $(-\infty,0]$, $0\le\chi'\le1$, and
$\chi(t)=t-c$ for $t\ge1$. The functions
\[
 \psi_N=\chi(\log|A|+N)
\]
extend smoothly by zero near the zeros of $A$ and are ordinary smooth
psh: away from those zeros $A$ is a unit moment, and at each zero the
cap is locally constant.

Fix $0<\delta<r^2/4$ and choose $\epsilon_N>0$ such that
$\delta+\epsilon_N\sup\psi_N<r^2/2$ on the closed polyannulus.
Then
\[
 w_N=\max(\rho_a,\delta+\epsilon_N\psi_N)-\rho_a
\]
extends by zero to a member of $\mathcal C$. The strict boundary
inequality supplies a collar where it is zero, and smooth soft maxima
give the required locally uniform psh approximation. On the fixed
smaller neighborhood $\rho_a<\delta/2$ one has
$\theta_{w_N}=\epsilon_N\DD\psi_N$. Lemma\ref{annihilate} gives
$\DD(d\DD\psi_N)=0$ there.

CLD16.7.3 applies to the regular holomorphic $A$ on the smooth,
pure-dimensional, boundaryless torus chart:
\[
 \DD[\log|A|]=\delta_{\operatorname{div}A}.
\]
The lower-dimensional support fact used in its immediate proof says
that compact smooth top-degree tests avoid $\{A=0\}$.
On such a test support, $\psi_N-N=\log|A|-c$ for all sufficiently large
$N$. Thus the positive currents $\DD\psi_N$ converge weakly to the
actual divisor current. CLD8.5.1 with the continuous coefficient $d$,
followed by continuous differentiation of currents, proves
\[
 \DD(d\delta_{\operatorname{div}A})=0
\]
on the smaller neighborhood. Covering the divisor proves the local
identity everywhere in every chart; off the divisor it is automatic.
The argument does not assert closedness of $d\delta_{\operatorname{div}A}$.

\section{Rational-domain approximation with controlled denominators}
Here is the neighborhood point needed below. The ordinary topology of
an affinoid spectrum is the initial topology of its absolute-value
functions. Around a point in the interior of a polyannulus, choose
finitely many strict lower and upper bounds defining a neighborhood
contained in the prescribed open set. Move the endpoints slightly
inwards, keeping the point inside. Bounds of the form $|s|^{m/n}$ are
dense among positive real bounds, so every chosen constraint can be
written using an integral power of its function and a scalar in $K$.
Weierstrass upper constraints have denominator one. For the finitely
many positive lower constraints $|h_i|\ge a_i$, use common denominator
$h_0=\prod_i h_i$, numerators $h_0/h_i$, and add numerator one with
the redundant bound $1\le(\prod_i a_i)^{-1}|h_0|$. The added numerator
ensures the unit-ideal condition and excludes every zero of $h_0$;
on its complement the other inequalities are exactly the lower
constraints. Upper constraints multiply their numerators by $h_0$.
This gives a rational domain contained in the chosen neighborhood and
having the point in its ordinary interior. Integral powers realize
the scalar bounds in the ordinary strict presentation when needed.
Thus shrinking to such a compact rational neighborhood is justified
in the ordinary topology, not merely by a rigid admissible cover.

\begin{lemma}\label{rational}
Let $V$ be a rational domain in a compact torus polyannulus $P$, and
$F\in\mathcal O(V)$. There are rational functions
$F_n=A_n/Q_n$, with Laurent-polynomial numerators and denominators,
such that $Q_n$ is a unit on $V$ and $F_n\to F$ uniformly on $V$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write the defining presentation as
\[
 \mathcal O(V)=\mathcal O(P)\langle r_i^{-1}T_i\rangle/
                    (g_0T_i-g_i),
\]
where $g_0,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ generate the unit ideal and the domain is
defined by $|g_i|\le r_i|g_0|$. These inequalities and the unit-ideal
condition imply that $g_0$ has no zero on $V$. It is a unit there and
has a positive lower absolute-value bound by compactness.
Finite polynomials in $T_i$ with coefficients in $\mathcal O(P)$
approximate $F$. Each such expression is a finite sum of products of
the $g_i/g_0$ and finitely many coefficients. Laurent polynomials are
dense in the polyannulus algebra by its completed-series definition.
Approximate these finitely many coefficients and all $g_i$ on $P$.
Choose the approximation $q$ to $g_0$ with
$\|q-g_0\|_V<\inf_V|g_0|$. Then $|q|=|g_0|$ on $V$, and $q$ is a
unit there. Substitution in the fixed finite expression is continuous
in the uniform norm, because inverse denominators have this fixed
positive lower bound. Clearing a finite power of $q$ gives a quotient
$A/q^m$ of Laurent polynomials. Choosing each finite truncation and
its substitutions with error tending to zero proves the assertion.
No uniform bound on the degrees or on the denominator powers is needed.
\end{proof}

\section{All local principal analytic divisor tests}
\begin{theorem}\label{localdiv}
Let $u,v\in\mathcal C$ satisfy $\MA(u)=\MA(v)$, and let $W$ be an
ordinary open subset of a torus chart. For every regular holomorphic
function $F$ on $W$,
\[
 \DD\bigl((u-v)\delta_{\operatorname{div}F}\bigr)=0
                      \quad\text{on }W.
\]
This includes local analytic hypersurfaces not defined by a Laurent
polynomial on the entire torus.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Shrink around any point to the interior of a compact rational domain
$V\subset W$ in a polyannulus. Lemma\ref{rational} gives
$F_n=A_n/Q_n\to F$ uniformly. After omitting initial terms the numerator
is nonzero. A nonzero Laurent polynomial is regular on the smooth
torus, and $Q_n$ is a unit on $V$. Poincare--Lelong therefore gives the
positive current identity on its interior
\[
 T_n=\DD[\log|F_n|]
       =\delta_{\operatorname{div}A_n}.
\]
The preceding section gives $\DD(dT_n)=0$ there, where $d=u-v$.

For any compact smooth $(2,2)$ test $\alpha$ in this interior, its
support avoids the lower-dimensional zero locus of the regular $F$.
Hence $m_\alpha=\inf_{\operatorname{supp}\alpha}|F|>0$. Uniform
approximation implies $|F_n-F|<m_\alpha$ on that support for all late
$n$. The ultrametric inequality gives $|F_n|=|F|$ there. The currents
$[\log|F_n|]$ therefore agree with $[\log|F|]$ on each such test for
all sufficiently late $n$, and converge weakly. Differentiation and
Poincare--Lelong yield
\[
 T_n\longrightarrow\DD[\log|F|]
                          =\delta_{\operatorname{div}F}.
\]
These are positive currents. CLD8.5.1 now gives
$dT_n\to d\delta_{\operatorname{div}F}$, because $d$ is bounded
continuous. Differentiating and using $\DD(dT_n)=0$ proves the result
on the interior of $V$. The local assertions glue on $W$.
\end{proof}
This passage uses approximation on a rational neighborhood and
invertibility of its denominators. It makes no assertion that an
arbitrary analytic curve map has a local closed hypersurface image,
or that the current identity automatically survives every scalar
extension. The weighting step is not licensed for an unbounded
generated difference without a separate integrability theorem.

\section{An exact sufficient recognition criterion}
Gubler--Rabinoff Definition7.1 and Propositions7.2--7.3, with
Theorems7.4 and7.6, concern $\PH$, the functions whose positive and
negative are both classically psh~\cite{GR}. Classical psh means tests
by all analytic curves after every analytic field extension. These
source results give continuity, local maximum and minimum principles,
and finite Shilov determination. They are existing source theorems,
not new uniqueness theorems for the present Monge--Ampere class.

\begin{corollary}\label{criterion}
If the bounded continuous difference $u-v$ in
Theorem\ref{localdiv} is locally classically pluriharmonic, it is
constant on $X$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Sheafiness makes it globally pluriharmonic. Compactness supplies a
global maximum. The maximum set is nonempty and closed by continuity,
and open by the local maximum principle at every point of the
boundaryless space. Connectedness makes it all of $X$.
\end{proof}

For completeness, this source framework also gives a finite-probe
compactness statement only for pluriharmonic defects. Cover a
quasicompact analytic space $Z$ by finitely many affinoid domains
$V_i$, and let $\Gamma$ be the union of their finite Shilov boundaries.
The map $h\mapsto(h(\xi))_{\xi\in\Gamma}$ embeds $\PH(Z)$ in
$\mathbb R^\Gamma$, and
\[
 \|h\|_{C(Z)}=\max_{\xi\in\Gamma}|h(\xi)|.
\]
Its image is a finite-dimensional linear subspace, hence closed.
Every bounded family is relatively compact in the uniform norm.
More precisely, convergence of a net on this finite set to a finite
vector implies uniform convergence to a unique pluriharmonic function:
the vector belongs to the closed image and the displayed norm measures
the convergence. No continuity assumption on a separately proposed
pointwise limit is needed. This is a direct finite-dimensional
consequence of the stated source maximum principles.

\title{Bounded continuous Monge--Ampere uniqueness\\by coordinate curves and Gauss rays}
\author{Working paper; independent review pending}
